## 9. Can Routes A, B, C be generalised? (round `011`, 2026-10-12)

**Answer: the theorem cores already are.** A new folder
[`research/twin-prime-parity/011/`](research/twin-prime-parity/011) audits the 010 routes against
four readings of "generalise" and finds that the first reading is already satisfied, because the 010
theorems were written at the right level:

* `exists_unique_root_of_sign_change` is `∀ f : ℝ → ℝ` — no arithmetic at all;
* `turing_reduction` is `∀ Finset α`, `α` arbitrary — pure combinatorics;
* `routeB_reduction_general` is `∀ f : ℂ → ℂ`, with only *analyticity on the rectangle*, a
  *functional equation* `f(1−s) = f(s)`, *conjugation reality* `f(conj s) = conj(f s)`, and zero data
  — `ζ` never appears in a hypothesis;
* `validated_truncation_bound` is a triangle inequality for any decomposition (generalised here to
  `n` tails).

So the work is **instantiation**, not new mathematics: per object one supplies an interval evaluator
(Route A/C), a functional equation and reality (Route B), and an explicit formula (Route C).

**The refined finding (this is the interesting part).** Route B does *not* actually need the bare
self-duality `F(1−s) = F(s)`; it needs only the reflection `logDeriv F (1−s) = −logDeriv F(s)`, and that
survives `h(1−s) = ε·h(s)` for **every** nonzero `ε` — differentiating gives `−h′(1−s) = ε h′(s)`, and
the `ε` cancels in the quotient. The bare identity is *not* recoverable when `ε ≠ 1` (no constant
rescaling helps, since `logDeriv (c·F) = logDeriv F`). Consequently the **root number is not an
obstruction** to Route B, only to the cosmetic rewriting `F(1−s) = F(s)`. The Lean encodes both
interfaces: `SelfDualReal` and the more general `SelfDualRealUpToSign` /
`routeB_general_of_logDeriv`, with `logDeriv_one_sub_of_const_mul` proving the `ε`-cancellation.

**Concrete instantiation: Dirichlet `L`-functions.** Mathlib has `completedLFunction`,
`rootNumber`, `differentiableAt_completedLFunction` and the functional equation
`IsPrimitive.completedLFunction_one_sub`
(`Λ(1−s) = N^{s−1/2}·rootNumber χ·Λ_{χ⁻¹}(s)`). Round 011 **proves the normalisation**
`dirichletL_normalised_one_sub`: with `χ⁻¹ = χ` (real/quadratic character) the function
`h(s) = N^{s/2}Λ_χ(s)` satisfies `h(1−s) = rootNumber χ · h(s)` — the exponent bookkeeping being
`(1−s)/2 + (s−½) = s/2`. Via the `ε`-cancellation this delivers Route B's hypothesis. What remains is
**one substantive Mathlib gap** — conjugation reality
`∀ s, Λ_χ(conj s) = conj(Λ_χ s)` for real `χ`, absent from the `LSeries` files, though 010's proved
`completedRiemannZeta₀_conj` is a transcription template — plus a *proof-technical* `ε ∈ {±1}` case
split in the landed `routeB_for_dirichletL` (not mathematically necessary, per the paragraph above),
and of course an interval engine for a Dirichlet `L`, which does not exist.

**What cannot generalise.** (i) Any all-zeros conclusion: the hypotheses are finitely many enclosures,
so the routes certify finite windows; the all-zeros statement for an `L`-function is (G)RH. (ii) The
interval engine: `010/rigorous/` is engineered around `ζ`'s Dirichlet series and its singularity
structure. (iii) Route A's simplicity conclusion (a `k`-th order certificate is a genuine extension).
(iv) The archimedean budget outside the `Γ` family.

**Artifacts.** `011/README.md`; `011/index.html` (the paper, with two figures);
`011/notes/generalisation-analysis.md` (prose audit) and `011/notes/generality-lean.md` (Lean
inventory); `011/lean/Generic.lean` (namespace `RouteABC`: `SelfDualReal`, `routeB_of_selfDualReal`,
`SelfDualRealUpToSign`, `routeB_general_of_logDeriv`, `logDeriv_one_sub_of_const_mul`,
`CertifiedZero.exists_unique_root`, `validated_truncation_bound_finset`/`_three`,
`dirichletL_normalised_one_sub`, `dirichletCompleted_selfDual`, `dirichletCompleted_conj`,
`RootNumberSign`, `CompletedLFunctionConj`, `routeB_for_dirichletL`) plus `Axioms.lean`;
`011/verify/check_claims.py` (5 independent checks, `ALL CHECKS PASSED`); figures generated by
`lib/generality_figs.py`. Build `011/lean/check.sh --all` is **green**, and all eleven headline
theorems have footprint `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

### 3.5 J5 — xi-horn citations verified

**Status: `[x]` done.** The two outstanding `[ ]` items of `xi-horn/TODO.md` **A1** are

**Gentili–Struppa 2007.** *G. Gentili, D. C. Struppa, "A new theory of regular functions
of a quaternionic variable," Adv. Math. **216**(1) (2007) 279–301,
doi:[10.1016/j.aim.2007.05.010](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aim.2007.05.010).*
Title, authors and venue confirmed (the paper is cited as [1] by the follow-up and
indexed as Zbl 1124.30015); the Elsevier DOI resolves (paywalled). **The Representation
Formula quoted in [`xi-horn/CONTINUATION.md`](xi-horn/CONTINUATION.md) §8.1 as (26) is
correct**: the standard statement ([Colombo–Gentili–Sabadini–Struppa,
arXiv:0905.1861](https://arxiv.org/abs/0905.1861), *Extension results for slice regular
functions*, Thm 3.1, attributing it to Gentili–Struppa 2007 and to [5]) is
`f(x+yI) = ½[f(x+yJ) + f(x−yJ)] + I·½[J[f(x−yJ) − f(x+yJ)]]`, which expands to
`½[(1 − IJ) f(x+yJ) + (1 + IJ) f(x−yJ)]` — exactly (26). So the §8.1 argument that a
slice-regular function carries "exactly the information of a holomorphic function of one
complex variable" rests on a correctly quoted theorem.

**Connes.** *A. Connes, "Trace formula in noncommutative geometry and the zeros of the
Riemann zeta function," Selecta Math. **5** (1999), no. 1, 29–106* — the full
bibliographic data is **confirmed verbatim in the abstract of Connes–Consani** below
("Selecta Math. 5 (1999), no. 1, 29--106"). The three pulled papers are confirmed:

| paper | arXiv | status |
|---|---|---|
| Connes–Moscovici, *Prolate spheroidal operator and Zeta* | [2112.05500](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.05500) | **confirmed** — submitted 10 Dec 2021, 17 pp.; abstract: the restriction of `W` to the complement of `J` has negative eigenvalues whose ultraviolet behaviour reproduces the squares of the zeta zeros, with eigenfunctions in the Sonin space, fitting the proof of Weil positivity at the archimedean place |
| Connes–Consani, *Weil positivity and Trace formula, the archimedean place* | [2006.13771](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.13771) | **confirmed** — submitted 24 Jun 2020, 57 pp.; abstract cites the 1999 Selecta paper and states that "Weil positivity implies RH" in the general semi-local case |
| Connes, *Trace formula …* (1997 EDP early version) | pulled as `connes-1997-edp-trace-formula.pdf` | **confirmed present**; the 1999 Selecta bibliographic data is confirmed via the Connes–Consani abstract |

programme's O12 asked for a Lean statement of the parity principle "in the restricted
setting of weight families generated by small-prime residue conditions"; that family is
now *defined*, and the principle is a *theorem* in it.

**The family.** `sieveWeight D c n = ∑_{d∈D} c d · 1_{d∣n}` — the **sign-blind
linear-sieve weights**: fixed by finitely many divisibility conditions, with no
reference to `λ` or `Ω`.

**Theorems (all `#print axioms` = `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).**

| theorem | statement |
|---|---|
| `sieveLam_collapse` | `∑_{n≤N} w(n)λ(n) = ∑_{d∈D} c_d λ(d) · (∑_{m≤N/d} λ(m))` — the exact **parity collapse**: every sign-blind weight sees `λ` only through the one-point sums |
| `sieveLam_abs_le` | if the one-point sums are `≤ ε·M` for all `M ≤ N` then `\|∑_{n≤N} w(n)λ(n)\| ≤ (∑_d \|c_d\|)·ε·N` — the sieve multiplies the available decay, it cannot create its own |
| `sieveLam_vanishes` | **the parity principle**: if `∑_{m≤M} λ(m) = o(M)` (PNT = `k = 1` Chowla, carried as the explicit hypothesis `LiouvilleVanishes`), then **every** sign-blind weight has `∑_{n≤N} w(n)λ(n) = o(N)` |
| `corr_twist_two` | `∑_{n≤N} (λ(n)(−1)^n)(λ(n+2)(−1)^{n+2}) = ∑_{n≤N} λ(n)λ(n+2)` — the index-parity twist cancels identically (rh47's `0/10⁶`-mismatch identity, now proved) |

The collapse was cross-checked numerically on `1/π`-independent small cases
(`D = {2,3}`, `c = (5,−2)`, `N = 10, 37, 100`: both sides agree). **Honest reading:** this
formalises the *algebraic skeleton* of Selberg's parity obstruction — a bounded-depth
linear sieve cannot manufacture a `λ`-correlation — not the full quantitative
sieve-level statement; the `k = 1` Chowla/PNT input stays a hypothesis, exactly as
register item OP-2 (settled) and O13 (J6, deferred) record.

### 3.8 J8 — the rectangle argument principle for Route B / T8

**Status: `[x]` done.** New Lean module
[`Rh45/ArgumentPrinciple.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/010/lean/Rh45/ArgumentPrinciple.lean)
(added to `010/lean/check.sh --all` and to `Rh45.lean`; docs in
[`Rh45/ARGUMENT_PRINCIPLE.md`](research/twin-prime-parity/010/lean/Rh45/ARGUMENT_PRINCIPLE.md)).
Independently re-run here: **`./check.sh --all` 7/7 `[check] OK`, exit 0**
(`ArgumentPrinciple.lean` 25 s), `#print axioms` on the six headline theorems =
`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

**What was built.** The whole contour computation for `∮_{∂R}(s−a)^{-1} ds`, by hand,
with no homotopy/winding-number API: `Complex.log` antiderivatives on each of the four
edges (`integral_inv_horizontal`, `integral_inv_vertical_right`, `integral_inv_vertical_left`),
the two slit-plane `arg` jumps (`log_sub_log_neg`, `log_neg_sub_log`), and then

| theorem | statement |
|---|---|
| `rectBoundary_inv_of_mem` | `a` strictly inside `[0,1]×[t₀,t₁]` ⟹ `∮ (s−a)^{-1} = 2πi` |
| `rectBoundary_inv_of_notMem` | `a` outside the closed rectangle ⟹ `∮ (s−a)^{-1} = 0` |
| `logDeriv_prod_pow` | `logDeriv (C·∏(s−z)^{m z}) = ∑ m z·(s−z)^{-1}` |
| `argument_principle_factorized` | under a local factorisation `f =ᶠ C·∏(s−z)^{m z}` with all `z` strictly inside: `∮_{∂R} f'/f = 2πi·∑ m z` |
| `routeB_reduction_factorized` | discharges the former `hAP` hypothesis: `(rightPath (logDeriv f) t₀ t₁).im = π·∑ m z` |

The key technical device is that the left edge `Re s = 0` crosses the branch slit, so the
*shifted* antiderivative `log(a − iy)` (whose real part is `a.re > 0`) is used; with
`u₀ = a − it₀` (`Im > 0`), `u₁ = a − it₁` (`Im < 0`) the four edge values telescope to
`iπ + iπ = 2πi`.

**Follow-up landed after the first pass: the Weierstrass step.** New module
[`Rh45/Weierstrass.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/010/lean/Rh45/Weierstrass.lean)
(536 lines, added to `010/lean/check.sh --all`; docs in
[`Rh45/WEIERSTRASS.md`](research/twin-prime-parity/010/lean/Rh45/WEIERSTRASS.md);
re-run here: **8/8 `[check] OK`, exit 0**, `#print axioms` on the four headline theorems =
`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, no `sorry`/`axiom`/`maxHeartbeats`, all
arithmetic as committed `linarith only […]` lists). **Route B now uses it:** a further
module [`Rh45/RouteBGeneral.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/010/lean/Rh45/RouteBGeneral.lean)
proves `routeB_reduction_general`,
`(rightPath (logDeriv f) t₀ t₁).im = π·∑_{z∈Z} m z`, from analyticity of `f`, its zero data
on the rectangle, and the two structural identities alone — no factorisation hypothesis and
no constant `C`. `routeB_reduction_factorized` is kept for compatibility and marked
superseded; `010/lean/check.sh --all` is now **9/9 green** and `routeB_reduction_general` is
axiom-clean. It supplies exactly the ingredient the first pass had named as missing:

| theorem | statement |
|---|---|
| `exists_factorization` | if `f` is analytic on a neighbourhood of the closed rectangle and its only zeros there are the points of a finite `Z` (interior, orders `m`), then `f = g · ∏_{z∈Z}(s−z)^{m z}` with `g` analytic **and nowhere zero** on the closed rectangle |
| `rectBoundary_logDeriv_eq_zero` | `g` analytic and nonvanishing there ⟹ `∮_{∂R} g′/g = 0` (Cauchy–Goursat for the rectangle, via `Complex.integral_boundary_rect_eq_zero_of_differentiableOn` at `z = t₀i`, `w = 1 + t₁i`) |
| `argument_principle_of_factorization` | the argument principle from an explicit zero-free factor `g` |
| `argument_principle_general` | `∮_{∂R} f′/f = 2πi·Σ_{z∈Z} m z` **with no factorisation hypothesis** — `exists_factorization` is applied inside |

**How the factorisation is built.** At each `z ∈ Z` the order is finite (otherwise `f`
would vanish on a punctured neighbourhood, contradicting the no-other-zeros hypothesis), so
Mathlib's local order factorisation `AnalyticAt.analyticOrderAt_ne_top` gives `h z` analytic
at `z` with `h z z ≠ 0` and `f =ᶠ[𝓝 z] (·−z)^{m z}·h z`. The glued factor is
`g s := if s ∈ Z then h s s / ∏_{z'≠s}(s−z')^{m z'} else f s / ∏_{z'∈Z}(s−z')^{m z'}`;
analyticity and nonvanishing are checked pointwise (at `z ∈ Z` via the eventual identity
`g =ᶠ h z/∏_{z'≠z}(·−z')^{m z'}`), and the product identity holds because both sides are
eventually equal at each zero and analytic. The argument principle then separates
`logDeriv f = logDeriv g + Σ m z/(·−z)` (product rule, `logDeriv_prod_pow`), kills the first
term by the Cauchy–Goursat lemma, and evaluates the second by the already-proved
`rectBoundary_inv_of_mem` (= `2πi`).

**What is *still* not claimed.** The zero set is still an input (`Z : Finset` plus "no other
zeros"), not derived from analyticity + compactness; the instance `f = ξ` additionally needs
an analytic `xi` on the rectangle (the `RouteBAnalytic` `xi` has removable singularities at
`0,1`), the reality `ξ(conj s) = conj(ξ s)`, and the zero-set identification — all
pre-existing gaps, not argument-principle or factorisation issues. No statement is made for
zeros on `∂R`. One hypothesis is genuinely needed and is made explicit in
`argument_principle_of_factorization`: analyticity of `f` on the rectangle, because
`logDeriv f` involves `deriv f`, a germ condition that pointwise `f = g·P` on the closed
rectangle does not determine (the requested literal signature without it is false — modify
`f` smoothly outside the rectangle).

### 3.9 J7 — the threshold-form fourth-order expansion

**Status: `[x]` done.** New Lean module
[`Op56/PhiFifth.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/open/lean/Op56/PhiFifth.lean) (added to
`open/lean/check.sh --all` and to `Op56.lean`). Independently re-run here:
**`./check.sh --all` 10/10 `[check] OK`, exit 0** (`PhiFifth.lean` 230 s, the rest
~200 s total), and `#print axioms Op56.threshold_fourth_order_uniform` =
`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

**Landed (all proved).** The cubic exponential remainder `exp_sub_three_bound`; the
third-order Taylor expansion `PhiS_taylor3_at_log2`
(`ΦS(u) = 6 − 26δ + 75δ² − (541/3)δ³ + O(δ⁴)`, `δ = u − log 2`); the reusable moment
identity `tsum_quad_poly_log2`; the cubic expansion `uPhiS_expansion_fourth`; the
`D`/`SFourth` definitions; the general first-order moment expansion
`tsum_pow_exp_first_order` / `PhiK_diff_linear_le`; `D_first_order` (exact
`D′(L) = −26/3 + (175/2)L − (541/4)L²`); `EFourth_diff_le`; the model lemmas
`SFourth_model`, `tM_lipschitz`, `tg_lipschitz_wide`, `log_thh_bound`; and the headline

```lean
theorem threshold_fourth_order_uniform :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop, ∀ u : ℝ, 1/2 ≤ u → u ≤ 1 →
      IsThreshold n (u*(n:ℝ)) →
        |u - Real.log 2 - 3*Real.log 2/(2*(n:ℝ))
            - (3*Real.log 2^2 - (25/12)*Real.log 2)/(n:ℝ)^2
            - ((73*Real.log 2 - 244*Real.log 2^2 + 200*Real.log 2^3)/8)/(n:ℝ)^3|
          ≤ C/(n:ℝ)^4
```

**The mathematics (exact, two routes, numerically confirmed).** Let `L = log 2`,
`δ = u − L`, `ΦS(u) = Σ_k k²e^{-uk}`, `ΦKp(u) = Σ_k k^p e^{-uk}`,
`D(u) = −(u/3)ΦK3(u) + (u²/8)ΦK4(u)`, `EFourth(u) = (u/4)ΦK4(u) − (u²/6)ΦK5(u) + (u³/48)ΦK6(u)`.
The threshold equation `Φ_{un}(n) = 1` with `Phi_fourth_order` gives
`F(L+δ) = uΦS(u)/(2n) + D(u)/n² + E(u)/n³ + O(n^{-4})`, `F(u) = 1 − 1/(e^u−1)`, and
substituting `δ = a₁/n + a₂/n² + a₃/n³` yields the exact coefficients

| coefficient | closed form | value |
|---|---|---|
| `a₁` | `3L/2` | `1.0397207708…` |
| `a₂` | `3L² − (25/12)L` | `−0.002697584411948…` (= the known OP-5 `c`) |
| `a₃` | `(73L − 244L² + 200L³)/8` | `−0.003232602172406…` (**new**) |

Two independent derivations agree ([`lib/op56_fourth.py`](lib/op56_fourth.py): moment
route and exact-`e^{-u}` closed-form route), and 60-digit Newton solutions of
`Φ_{un}(n)=1` for `n = 10^4,10^5,10^6` give `n³(u − L − a₁/n − a₂/n²) → a₃`, with
Richardson extrapolation matching `a₃` to `3·10⁻¹⁵`.

**Note on the Lean arithmetic style.** The remaining arithmetic goals in the headline
assembly were closed following [`linarith-agent-prompt.md`](research/twin-prime-parity/linarith-agent-prompt.md)
(committed `linarith only [ … ]` lists on cleaned goals, named sign facts, no retry
ladder). Two `set_option maxHeartbeats` directives and some bare `linarith`/`nlinarith`
calls remain in the pre-existing body of `PhiFifth.lean`; removing them requires
restructuring eight tactics that time out at the default budget, and is recorded as
follow-up polish rather than silently left unmentioned. The build is green, `sorry`-free
and `axiom`-free.

### 5.1 The `rh40` round-01 `p(L)` attack — `OP-34`, `OP-35`, `OP-36`, `OP-37`

Full report: [`research/attacks/OP-34-36-37-35.md`](research/attacks/OP-34-36-37-35.md);
helpers [`lib/tpp_window_collision.py`](lib/tpp_window_collision.py) (self-test 7/7, exit 0,
re-run here) and [`research/attacks/validate_op34.py`](research/attacks/validate_op34.py).

* **OP-34 + OP-36 — the `[DREAM]` class sum is REFUTED, the exact criterion is PROVED.**
  The "sum over `(i,j)` classes of their window counts" over-counts `p(L)` on exactly
  **604/1399** `L` for `x = 1/π`; the source's literal
  `1 + #{} + Σ_{i≤j}T(i,j)` over-counts on **all 1399** (`T(i,j)` counts last-index `≤ j`,
  so each window is counted `m−J+1` times). Cause: the classes are **not disjoint** — the
  same 604 `L`. The corrected criterion is
  `factor(t) = factor(t') ⟺ x(t) = x(t') ∧ shape(t) = shape(t')` with
  `x = a_i − t`, `shape = (0, a_{i+1}−a_i, …, a_j−a_i)`, and the corrected exact formula
  `p(L) = [∃ all-zero] + Σ_shapes |⋃_{C: shape} X(C)|` — group by **gap-run shape** and take
  the **union** of offset intervals `X(i,j)` (given in the report). Validated on
  **6 378 064** exhaustive cases (`m+1 ≤ 4`, `N ≤ 31`), 1 248 945 class pairs, plus every
  `L` of `1/π`, `log 2`, `N = 13000`, `√2−1`, `e−2`: **0 mismatches**.
* **OP-37(a) realisability — PROVED.** Realised `(i,x)` is exactly
  `max(0, a_i − (N−L)) ≤ x ≤ min(d_{i−1}−1, a_i, L−1)`; the survey's 95 826/0 reproduced.
* **OP-37(b) all-zero — source REFUTED, corrected form PROVED.** Witness `((0,4), N=6, L=3)`
  (independently reproduced here: an all-zero window exists but the source criterion says
  not). The correct criterion is `L ≤ max(a_0, max_j(d_j−1), N−1−a_m)` — the source is wrong
  on 24 337/95 826 cases, the corrected form on 0.
* **OP-37(c) injectivity — source REFUTED, corrected form PROVED (stronger than surveyed).**
  Witness `((12,20), N=26, L=12)` (reproduced: `(0,7),(1,7)` share the factor `(7,)`).
  Corrected: `p(L) ≥ a_m + 2 ⟹` the window→factor map is injective, **with no `N`
  hypothesis** (proof: every nonempty window starts at `t ≤ a_m`, so there are at most
  `a_m+1` of them; a collision forces `p ≤ a_m+1`). Machine-checked as
  `Rh40.injOn_of_card_ge` in
  [`rounds/rh40/lean/Rh40/Plateau.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/rounds/rh40/lean/Rh40/Plateau.lean);
  `./check.sh --all` **2/2 green, exit 0** (re-run here: `Plateau.lean` 37 s, root 21 s).
  Checked on 463 771 plateau / 704 632 conditional / 15 087 survey-loop cases, 0 violations.
* **OP-35 — REFUTED / undefined.** `S_{1,k}` is **undefined corpus-wide** (two prose
  mentions; the `d_j` indexing is also unfixed). The natural reading `S_{1,k} = Σ_{i≤k} d_i`
  gives `D(L) = (L−12)_+` for `1/π`, switching on at `L = 13`, whereas the measured `2→1`
  slope drop is at `L = 14` (`p(13)=16, p(14)=18, p(15)=19`). No partial-sum convention
  repairs it (it would need `S_{1,−1} = 1`), and the natural `D` is unbounded while a
  cancelled-pair deficit must be bounded.

*Honest caveat (from the attack):* the injectivity theorem is stated conditionally on
`p(L) ≥ a_m + 2`; the harvested plateau *value* `max p = a_m + 2` is still unproved and is
used only to instantiate it.

### 5.2 The residual-orbit attack — `OP-28`, `OP-30`, `OP-33`

Full report: [`research/attacks/OP-28-30-33.md`](research/attacks/OP-28-30-33.md); helper
[`lib/tpp_no_limit_orbit.py`](lib/tpp_no_limit_orbit.py) (self-test 5/5, exit 0, re-run
here); compute script [`research/attacks/op28_30_33_compute.py`](research/attacks/op28_30_33_compute.py).

* **OP-28 ≡ OP-30 — the no-limit family is PROVED (constructive).** There exist `x ∈ (0,1)`
  and a greedy orbit with `limsup_K (1/K)Σ_{k<K} log c_k ≥ −0.76` and `liminf_K ≤ −1.21`,
  so the running mean has **no limit**. Construction: prescribe `α_k` alternating `1/2, 1/4`
  in blocks `M_j = 3^j` (exact target `α_k = (q_k²+2q_k)/q_{k+1}`), build `q_k` **backwards**
  by the exact inverse `u_k = n_k u_{k+1}/(n_k + u_{k+1})` (`n_k = q_k+2`, `u = 1/r`), and
  take `x = Σ_{k≥1} 1/(q_k+2)`. Rigour: each backward bracket lies inside its digit cell
  `(q_k+1, q_k+2]` (verified exactly), the backward map is a contraction with
  `|s_k − α_k| ≤ η_k` and `Ση_k ≤ 1.6·10⁻³` (exact-rational recursion), and the block-end
  running means of `log α_k` form an exact 2-cycle with gap `0.35–0.52 ≫ 10⁻³`. Exact
  witness `x = 300129656263973531720568953662090234 / 48845289055200132283765298144075427525`
  realises `q_1..q_4`. *(The survey's squaring law and `q_{k+1} = ⌊q_k²/α_k⌋` were re-derived:
  both correct, the latter to leading order only; the exact self-consistent target is the
  `α_k` above.)*
* **OP-33(a) — the precision floor is PROVED, and closed in Lean here.** If `r` is
  nonnegative, `r_0 ≤ 1/10`, `r_{k+1} ≤ r_k²`, and `10^{−D} < r_{K−1}`, then `2^{K−1} ≤ D`
  — a forward orbit at `D` decimal digits can run only `K ≤ log₂ D + 1` steps. The attack
  left this as a non-compiling WIP file; it is now landed and axiom-clean as
  `Rh42.step_bound` in
  [`rounds/rh42/lean/Rh42/PrecisionFloor.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/rounds/rh42/lean/Rh42/PrecisionFloor.lean),
  wired into `check.sh --all` and `Rh42.lean` (`./check.sh --all` **5/5 green, exit 0**),
  `#print axioms` = `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`. The source's
  "7–13 steps before underflow" (measured `D = 50…3000 → 6…12`) is therefore a **theorem,
  not a bug**.
* **OP-33(b) — EVIDENCE.** Means of `log c_k` over `10⁴` prescribed (backward-realised)
  steps converge to the mean of `log α_k`: `−0.6931` (`1/2`), `−1.3863` (`1/4`), `−2.3026`
  (`1/10`), `−0.7557` (the survey's `10^j` blocks). **None is `−1`**; the source's claim is
  confirmed but re-attributed — no universal limit exists, and the finite-`K` mean is
  strictly below the `s`-mean by the un-decayed gap `Γ_K/K`, so at `K ≤ 15` no convergence
  can be read off.

## 7. Bridging the last `010/lean` Mathlib gap (2026-10-12)

**Status: `[x]` done — the polygamma/Hurwitz series is now proved, so the archimedean
input of the round is unconditional for `k ≥ 1`.** The `Rh45` build is **13/13
`[check] OK`, exit 0**, with **0 `sorry`, 0 `axiom`, 0 `admit`, 0 `native_decide`, no
`maxHeartbeats`**; `#print axioms` on every headline theorem is
`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

**The gap.** `Rh45.archimedean_deriv_bound_of_digamma_series` took as its only
hypothesis the Euler–Maclaurin/Hurwitz series
`ψ^{(k)}(z) = (−1)^{k+1} k! Σ_{j≥0}(z+j)^{−k−1}`, hence
`‖ψ^{(k)}(1/4+it/2)‖ ≤ k! Σ_j (1/4+j)^{−k−1}`. Mathlib's `Complex.digamma` carried
only the recurrence/reflection/duplication identities.

**Two new modules.**

* [`Rh45/GammaProduct.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/010/lean/Rh45/GammaProduct.lean)
  (the crux). Mathlib has the complex Gauss product **pointwise**
  (`Complex.GammaSeq`, `Complex.GammaSeq_tendsto_Gamma`) but no locally uniform
  version, hence no way to differentiate the limit. The module proves
  `analyticAt_GammaSeq`, the uniform bound `‖GammaSeq s n‖ ≤ Γ(re s)` (via the integral
  representation, *not* the crude `n^s n!/∏` bound — the latter is not uniform on a
  circle), **`tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn_GammaSeq`** (`GammaSeq · n → Γ` locally uniformly
  on `re s > 0`), then `tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn_deriv_GammaSeq`,
  `tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn_logDeriv_GammaSeq` (Weierstrass differentiation,
  `TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn.deriv`), and the finite identity
  `logDeriv (GammaSeq · n) s = log n − Σ_{j≤n}(s+j)⁻¹`. The local-uniform step is by the
  **circle-Cauchy route**: Cauchy's formula on `C(c,ρ)` bounds the discrepancy by
  `(2π)⁻¹ρ(ρ−r)⁻¹·A_n` with the *scalar* `A_n = ∫θ ‖GammaSeq·n − Γ‖(circleMap c ρ θ)`,
  and `A_n → 0` by dominated convergence on a finite-measure interval — so no
  Vitali/Montel theorem is needed. A companion note
  [`Rh45/GAMMA_PRODUCT.md`](research/twin-prime-parity/010/lean/Rh45/GAMMA_PRODUCT.md)
  records it. (Mathlib's own docstring at `BohrMollerup.lean:29` points to
  `Complex.Gamma_seq_tendsto_Gamma`, a name that does not exist; the real object is
  `Complex.GammaSeq` in `Beta.lean`.)
* [`Rh45/PolygammaSeries.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/010/lean/Rh45/PolygammaSeries.lean).
  The explicit iterated derivative `iteratedDeriv_logDeriv_GammaSeq`
  (`deriv^[k](logDeriv (GammaSeq·n)) s = (−1)^{k+1} k! Σ_{j≤n}(s+j)^{−k−1}` for `k ≥ 1`),
  the **Gauss/Hurwitz series** `digamma_polygamma_series` (`HasSum`), summability
  `summable_polygamma_series`, the norm bound
  `norm_deriv_digamma_le : ‖ψ^{(k)}(s)‖ ≤ k! Σ_j (re s + j)^{−k−1}`, the specialisation
  `Rh45.digamma_series_bound` at `s = 1/4 + it/2`, and the **unconditional**
  `Rh45.archimedean_deriv_bound (k) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (t) : ‖Ψ^{(k)}(t)‖ ≤ psiSeriesBound k`.
  The conditional `archimedean_deriv_bound_of_digamma_series` is kept for compatibility.

**The `k = 0` case, handled honestly.** `Σ_j (1/4+j)^{−1}` diverges, so
`psiSeriesBound 0 = 0` (`Rh45.psiSeriesBound_zero`) and the `k = 0` instance of the
conditional theorem carries no information. A *valid* crude `k = 0` bound is supplied
instead, `Rh45.norm_digamma_le`, from the Weierstrass partial-sum form
`ψ(s) = −γ + Σ_j(1/(j+1) − (s+j)⁻¹)` plus `Real.tendsto_harmonic_sub_log`.

**Paper.** The whole bridge is written up as
[`research/twin-prime-parity/010/polygamma.html`](research/twin-prime-parity/010/polygamma.html)
(*The polygamma series, proved*), in the round's standard HTML style: abstract, contents,
the problem, definitions, the Mathlib inventory, the locally uniform Gauss product (with the
circle-Cauchy inequality and the scalar dominated-convergence argument), Weierstrass
differentiation, the polygamma series, the norm bound and the unconditional archimedean budget,
the `k = 0` diagnosis and replacement bound, a status table, and reproduction/references. It is
linked from `010/index.html` and from `010/lean/README.md`.

**Primer.** The three certification strategies are written up for a reader new to the
material as [`research/twin-prime-parity/010/routes-abc-primer.html`](research/twin-prime-parity/010/routes-abc-primer.html)
(*Routes A, B, C — a pedagogical guide*): what certifying a zero means, the Riemann–Siegel
`Z` dictionary, the three failure modes of naive computation, Route A (IVT + strict monotonicity +
simplicity, in enclosure form, with the `γ₁…γ₅` certificates), Route B (Turing's cardinality squeeze,
the rectangle/half-path `I₃` geometry, `N(T) = Im(I₃)/π`, and the three hypotheses — `hAP`, the
winding number, ξ reality/entireness — that are now theorems), Route C (the explicit-formula split,
Chebyshev prime tail, Simpson archimedean tail, the `9.08·10⁻⁹ ≤ 2.79·10⁻⁸` result), a
proved/certified/cited ledger, and the honest statement that RH is not addressed. Four SVG figures
generated by `lib/routes_figs.py`. Linked from `010/index.html`.

**Net effect on the round.** The archimedean derivative budget `‖Ψ^{(k)}(t)‖ ≤
psiSeriesBound k` is now a theorem for every `k ≥ 1` (`k = 1,…,4` are exactly the cases
the composite-Simpson assembly uses), and the `k = 0` slot has an explicit finite bound.
No hypothesis of `Archimedean.lean` remains unproved except the one that was previously
named and is now discharged; the full `Rh45` development is self-contained.

## 9. Can Routes A, B, C be generalised? (round `011`, 2026-10-12)

**Answer: the theorem cores already are.** A new folder
[`research/twin-prime-parity/011/`](research/twin-prime-parity/011) audits the 010 routes against
four readings of "generalise" and finds that the first reading is already satisfied, because the 010
theorems were written at the right level:

* `exists_unique_root_of_sign_change` is `∀ f : ℝ → ℝ` — no arithmetic at all;
* `turing_reduction` is `∀ Finset α`, `α` arbitrary — pure combinatorics;
* `routeB_reduction_general` is `∀ f : ℂ → ℂ`, with only *analyticity on the rectangle*, a
  *functional equation* `f(1−s) = f(s)`, *conjugation reality* `f(conj s) = conj(f s)`, and zero data
  — `ζ` never appears in a hypothesis;
* `validated_truncation_bound` is a triangle inequality for any decomposition (generalised here to
  `n` tails).

So the work is **instantiation**, not new mathematics: per object one supplies an interval evaluator
(Route A/C), a functional equation and reality (Route B), and an explicit formula (Route C).

**The refined finding (this is the interesting part).** Route B does *not* actually need the bare
self-duality `F(1−s) = F(s)`; it needs only the reflection `logDeriv F (1−s) = −logDeriv F(s)`, and that
survives `h(1−s) = ε·h(s)` for **every** nonzero `ε` — differentiating gives `−h′(1−s) = ε h′(s)`, and
the `ε` cancels in the quotient. The bare identity is *not* recoverable when `ε ≠ 1` (no constant
rescaling helps, since `logDeriv (c·F) = logDeriv F`). Consequently the **root number is not an
obstruction** to Route B, only to the cosmetic rewriting `F(1−s) = F(s)`. The Lean encodes both
interfaces: `SelfDualReal` and the more general `SelfDualRealUpToSign` /
`routeB_general_of_logDeriv`, with `logDeriv_one_sub_of_const_mul` proving the `ε`-cancellation.

**Concrete instantiation: Dirichlet `L`-functions.** Mathlib has `completedLFunction`,
`rootNumber`, `differentiableAt_completedLFunction` and the functional equation
`IsPrimitive.completedLFunction_one_sub`
(`Λ(1−s) = N^{s−1/2}·rootNumber χ·Λ_{χ⁻¹}(s)`). Round 011 **proves the normalisation**
`dirichletL_normalised_one_sub`: with `χ⁻¹ = χ` (real/quadratic character) the function
`h(s) = N^{s/2}Λ_χ(s)` satisfies `h(1−s) = rootNumber χ · h(s)` — the exponent bookkeeping being
`(1−s)/2 + (s−½) = s/2`. Via the `ε`-cancellation this delivers Route B's hypothesis. What remains is
**one substantive Mathlib gap** — conjugation reality
`∀ s, Λ_χ(conj s) = conj(Λ_χ s)` for real `χ`, absent from the `LSeries` files, though 010's proved
`completedRiemannZeta₀_conj` is a transcription template — plus a *proof-technical* `ε ∈ {±1}` case
split in the landed `routeB_for_dirichletL` (not mathematically necessary, per the paragraph above),
and of course an interval engine for a Dirichlet `L`, which does not exist.

**What cannot generalise.** (i) Any all-zeros conclusion: the hypotheses are finitely many enclosures,
so the routes certify finite windows; the all-zeros statement for an `L`-function is (G)RH. (ii) The
interval engine: `010/rigorous/` is engineered around `ζ`'s Dirichlet series and its singularity
structure. (iii) Route A's simplicity conclusion (a `k`-th order certificate is a genuine extension).
(iv) The archimedean budget outside the `Γ` family.

**Artifacts.** `011/README.md`; `011/index.html` (the paper, with two figures);
`011/notes/generalisation-analysis.md` (prose audit) and `011/notes/generality-lean.md` (Lean
inventory); `011/lean/Generic.lean` (namespace `RouteABC`: `SelfDualReal`, `routeB_of_selfDualReal`,
`SelfDualRealUpToSign`, `routeB_general_of_logDeriv`, `logDeriv_one_sub_of_const_mul`,
`CertifiedZero.exists_unique_root`, `validated_truncation_bound_finset`/`_three`,
`dirichletL_normalised_one_sub`, `dirichletCompleted_selfDual`, `dirichletCompleted_conj`,
`RootNumberSign`, `CompletedLFunctionConj`, `routeB_for_dirichletL`) plus `Axioms.lean`;
`011/verify/check_claims.py` (5 independent checks, `ALL CHECKS PASSED`); figures generated by
`lib/generality_figs.py`. Build `011/lean/check.sh --all` is **green**, and all eleven headline
theorems have footprint `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

### 3.5 J5 — xi-horn citations verified

**Status: `[x]` done.** The two outstanding `[ ]` items of `xi-horn/TODO.md` **A1** are
now verified.

**Gentili–Struppa 2007.** *G. Gentili, D. C. Struppa, "A new theory of regular functions
of a quaternionic variable," Adv. Math. **216**(1) (2007) 279–301,
doi:[10.1016/j.aim.2007.05.010](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aim.2007.05.010).*
Title, authors and venue confirmed (the paper is cited as [1] by the follow-up and
indexed as Zbl 1124.30015); the Elsevier DOI resolves (paywalled). **The Representation
Formula quoted in [`xi-horn/CONTINUATION.md`](xi-horn/CONTINUATION.md) §8.1 as (26) is
correct**: the standard statement ([Colombo–Gentili–Sabadini–Struppa,
arXiv:0905.1861](https://arxiv.org/abs/0905.1861), *Extension results for slice regular
functions*, Thm 3.1, attributing it to Gentili–Struppa 2007 and to [5]) is
`f(x+yI) = ½[f(x+yJ) + f(x−yJ)] + I·½[J[f(x−yJ) − f(x+yJ)]]`, which expands to
`½[(1 − IJ) f(x+yJ) + (1 + IJ) f(x−yJ)]` — exactly (26). So the §8.1 argument that a
slice-regular function carries "exactly the information of a holomorphic function of one
complex variable" rests on a correctly quoted theorem.

**Connes.** *A. Connes, "Trace formula in noncommutative geometry and the zeros of the
Riemann zeta function," Selecta Math. **5** (1999), no. 1, 29–106* — the full
bibliographic data is **confirmed verbatim in the abstract of Connes–Consani** below
("Selecta Math. 5 (1999), no. 1, 29--106"). The three pulled papers are confirmed:

| paper | arXiv | status |
|---|---|---|
| Connes–Moscovici, *Prolate spheroidal operator and Zeta* | [2112.05500](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.05500) | **confirmed** — submitted 10 Dec 2021, 17 pp.; abstract: the restriction of `W` to the complement of `J` has negative eigenvalues whose ultraviolet behaviour reproduces the squares of the zeta zeros, with eigenfunctions in the Sonin space, fitting the proof of Weil positivity at the archimedean place |
| Connes–Consani, *Weil positivity and Trace formula, the archimedean place* | [2006.13771](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.13771) | **confirmed** — submitted 24 Jun 2020, 57 pp.; abstract cites the 1999 Selecta paper and states that "Weil positivity implies RH" in the general semi-local case |
| Connes, *Trace formula …* (1997 EDP early version) | pulled as `connes-1997-edp-trace-formula.pdf` | **confirmed present**; the 1999 Selecta bibliographic data is confirmed via the Connes–Consani abstract |

All six PDFs named in `xi-horn/TODO.md` A1 are present in `xi-horn/`. **A1 is closed;
nothing in the Rust work or the mathematics depended on the open status.**

### 3.6 J9 — sign-blindness / the parity principle formalised (O12)

**Status: `[x]` done.** New Lean module
[`Rh47/Parity.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/rounds/rh47/lean/Rh47/Parity.lean)
(268 lines, added to `Rh47/lean/check.sh --all` and to `Rh47.lean`; `./check.sh --all`
is **3/3 green**, `Rh47/Sparse.lean` 5 s, `Rh47/Parity.lean` 31 s, root 26 s). The
programme's O12 asked for a Lean statement of the parity principle "in the restricted
setting of weight families generated by small-prime residue conditions"; that family is
now *defined*, and the principle is a *theorem* in it.

**The family.** `sieveWeight D c n = ∑_{d∈D} c d · 1_{d∣n}` — the **sign-blind
linear-sieve weights**: fixed by finitely many divisibility conditions, with no
reference to `λ` or `Ω`.

**Theorems (all `#print axioms` = `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).**

| theorem | statement |
|---|---|
| `sieveLam_collapse` | `∑_{n≤N} w(n)λ(n) = ∑_{d∈D} c_d λ(d) · (∑_{m≤N/d} λ(m))` — the exact **parity collapse**: every sign-blind weight sees `λ` only through the one-point sums |
| `sieveLam_abs_le` | if the one-point sums are `≤ ε·M` for all `M ≤ N` then `\|∑_{n≤N} w(n)λ(n)\| ≤ (∑_d \|c_d\|)·ε·N` — the sieve multiplies the available decay, it cannot create its own |
| `sieveLam_vanishes` | **the parity principle**: if `∑_{m≤M} λ(m) = o(M)` (PNT = `k = 1` Chowla, carried as the explicit hypothesis `LiouvilleVanishes`), then **every** sign-blind weight has `∑_{n≤N} w(n)λ(n) = o(N)` |
| `corr_twist_two` | `∑_{n≤N} (λ(n)(−1)^n)(λ(n+2)(−1)^{n+2}) = ∑_{n≤N} λ(n)λ(n+2)` — the index-parity twist cancels identically (rh47's `0/10⁶`-mismatch identity, now proved) |

The collapse was cross-checked numerically on `1/π`-independent small cases
(`D = {2,3}`, `c = (5,−2)`, `N = 10, 37, 100`: both sides agree). **Honest reading:** this
formalises the *algebraic skeleton* of Selberg's parity obstruction — a bounded-depth
linear sieve cannot manufacture a `λ`-correlation — not the full quantitative
sieve-level statement; the `k = 1` Chowla/PNT input stays a hypothesis, exactly as
register item OP-2 (settled) and O13 (J6, deferred) record.

### 3.8 J8 — the rectangle argument principle for Route B / T8

**Status: `[x]` done.** New Lean module
[`Rh45/ArgumentPrinciple.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/010/lean/Rh45/ArgumentPrinciple.lean)
(added to `010/lean/check.sh --all` and to `Rh45.lean`; docs in
[`Rh45/ARGUMENT_PRINCIPLE.md`](research/twin-prime-parity/010/lean/Rh45/ARGUMENT_PRINCIPLE.md)).
Independently re-run here: **`./check.sh --all` 7/7 `[check] OK`, exit 0**
(`ArgumentPrinciple.lean` 25 s), `#print axioms` on the six headline theorems =
`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

**What was built.** The whole contour computation for `∮_{∂R}(s−a)^{-1} ds`, by hand,
with no homotopy/winding-number API: `Complex.log` antiderivatives on each of the four
edges (`integral_inv_horizontal`, `integral_inv_vertical_right`, `integral_inv_vertical_left`),
the two slit-plane `arg` jumps (`log_sub_log_neg`, `log_neg_sub_log`), and then

| theorem | statement |
|---|---|
| `rectBoundary_inv_of_mem` | `a` strictly inside `[0,1]×[t₀,t₁]` ⟹ `∮ (s−a)^{-1} = 2πi` |
| `rectBoundary_inv_of_notMem` | `a` outside the closed rectangle ⟹ `∮ (s−a)^{-1} = 0` |
| `logDeriv_prod_pow` | `logDeriv (C·∏(s−z)^{m z}) = ∑ m z·(s−z)^{-1}` |
| `argument_principle_factorized` | under a local factorisation `f =ᶠ C·∏(s−z)^{m z}` with all `z` strictly inside: `∮_{∂R} f'/f = 2πi·∑ m z` |
| `routeB_reduction_factorized` | discharges the former `hAP` hypothesis: `(rightPath (logDeriv f) t₀ t₁).im = π·∑ m z` |

The key technical device is that the left edge `Re s = 0` crosses the branch slit, so the
*shifted* antiderivative `log(a − iy)` (whose real part is `a.re > 0`) is used; with
`u₀ = a − it₀` (`Im > 0`), `u₁ = a − it₁` (`Im < 0`) the four edge values telescope to
`iπ + iπ = 2πi`.

**Follow-up landed after the first pass: the Weierstrass step.** New module
[`Rh45/Weierstrass.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/010/lean/Rh45/Weierstrass.lean)
(536 lines, added to `010/lean/check.sh --all`; docs in
[`Rh45/WEIERSTRASS.md`](research/twin-prime-parity/010/lean/Rh45/WEIERSTRASS.md);
re-run here: **8/8 `[check] OK`, exit 0**, `#print axioms` on the four headline theorems =
`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, no `sorry`/`axiom`/`maxHeartbeats`, all
arithmetic as committed `linarith only […]` lists). **Route B now uses it:** a further
module [`Rh45/RouteBGeneral.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/010/lean/Rh45/RouteBGeneral.lean)
proves `routeB_reduction_general`,
`(rightPath (logDeriv f) t₀ t₁).im = π·∑_{z∈Z} m z`, from analyticity of `f`, its zero data
on the rectangle, and the two structural identities alone — no factorisation hypothesis and
no constant `C`. `routeB_reduction_factorized` is kept for compatibility and marked
superseded; `010/lean/check.sh --all` is now **9/9 green** and `routeB_reduction_general` is
axiom-clean. It supplies exactly the ingredient the first pass had named as missing:

| theorem | statement |
|---|---|
| `exists_factorization` | if `f` is analytic on a neighbourhood of the closed rectangle and its only zeros there are the points of a finite `Z` (interior, orders `m`), then `f = g · ∏_{z∈Z}(s−z)^{m z}` with `g` analytic **and nowhere zero** on the closed rectangle |
| `rectBoundary_logDeriv_eq_zero` | `g` analytic and nonvanishing there ⟹ `∮_{∂R} g′/g = 0` (Cauchy–Goursat for the rectangle, via `Complex.integral_boundary_rect_eq_zero_of_differentiableOn` at `z = t₀i`, `w = 1 + t₁i`) |
| `argument_principle_of_factorization` | the argument principle from an explicit zero-free factor `g` |
| `argument_principle_general` | `∮_{∂R} f′/f = 2πi·Σ_{z∈Z} m z` **with no factorisation hypothesis** — `exists_factorization` is applied inside |

**How the factorisation is built.** At each `z ∈ Z` the order is finite (otherwise `f`
would vanish on a punctured neighbourhood, contradicting the no-other-zeros hypothesis), so
Mathlib's local order factorisation `AnalyticAt.analyticOrderAt_ne_top` gives `h z` analytic
at `z` with `h z z ≠ 0` and `f =ᶠ[𝓝 z] (·−z)^{m z}·h z`. The glued factor is
`g s := if s ∈ Z then h s s / ∏_{z'≠s}(s−z')^{m z'} else f s / ∏_{z'∈Z}(s−z')^{m z'}`;
analyticity and nonvanishing are checked pointwise (at `z ∈ Z` via the eventual identity
`g =ᶠ h z/∏_{z'≠z}(·−z')^{m z'}`), and the product identity holds because both sides are
eventually equal at each zero and analytic. The argument principle then separates
`logDeriv f = logDeriv g + Σ m z/(·−z)` (product rule, `logDeriv_prod_pow`), kills the first
term by the Cauchy–Goursat lemma, and evaluates the second by the already-proved
`rectBoundary_inv_of_mem` (= `2πi`).

**What is *still* not claimed.** The zero set is still an input (`Z : Finset` plus "no other
zeros"), not derived from analyticity + compactness; the instance `f = ξ` additionally needs
an analytic `xi` on the rectangle (the `RouteBAnalytic` `xi` has removable singularities at
`0,1`), the reality `ξ(conj s) = conj(ξ s)`, and the zero-set identification — all
pre-existing gaps, not argument-principle or factorisation issues. No statement is made for
zeros on `∂R`. One hypothesis is genuinely needed and is made explicit in
`argument_principle_of_factorization`: analyticity of `f` on the rectangle, because
`logDeriv f` involves `deriv f`, a germ condition that pointwise `f = g·P` on the closed
rectangle does not determine (the requested literal signature without it is false — modify
`f` smoothly outside the rectangle).

### 3.9 J7 — the threshold-form fourth-order expansion

**Status: `[x]` done.** New Lean module
[`Op56/PhiFifth.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/open/lean/Op56/PhiFifth.lean) (added to
`open/lean/check.sh --all` and to `Op56.lean`). Independently re-run here:
**`./check.sh --all` 10/10 `[check] OK`, exit 0** (`PhiFifth.lean` 230 s, the rest
~200 s total), and `#print axioms Op56.threshold_fourth_order_uniform` =
`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

**Landed (all proved).** The cubic exponential remainder `exp_sub_three_bound`; the
third-order Taylor expansion `PhiS_taylor3_at_log2`
(`ΦS(u) = 6 − 26δ + 75δ² − (541/3)δ³ + O(δ⁴)`, `δ = u − log 2`); the reusable moment
identity `tsum_quad_poly_log2`; the cubic expansion `uPhiS_expansion_fourth`; the
`D`/`SFourth` definitions; the general first-order moment expansion
`tsum_pow_exp_first_order` / `PhiK_diff_linear_le`; `D_first_order` (exact
`D′(L) = −26/3 + (175/2)L − (541/4)L²`); `EFourth_diff_le`; the model lemmas
`SFourth_model`, `tM_lipschitz`, `tg_lipschitz_wide`, `log_thh_bound`; and the headline

```lean
theorem threshold_fourth_order_uniform :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop, ∀ u : ℝ, 1/2 ≤ u → u ≤ 1 →
      IsThreshold n (u*(n:ℝ)) →
        |u - Real.log 2 - 3*Real.log 2/(2*(n:ℝ))
            - (3*Real.log 2^2 - (25/12)*Real.log 2)/(n:ℝ)^2
            - ((73*Real.log 2 - 244*Real.log 2^2 + 200*Real.log 2^3)/8)/(n:ℝ)^3|
          ≤ C/(n:ℝ)^4
```

**The mathematics (exact, two routes, numerically confirmed).** Let `L = log 2`,
`δ = u − L`, `ΦS(u) = Σ_k k²e^{-uk}`, `ΦKp(u) = Σ_k k^p e^{-uk}`,
`D(u) = −(u/3)ΦK3(u) + (u²/8)ΦK4(u)`, `EFourth(u) = (u/4)ΦK4(u) − (u²/6)ΦK5(u) + (u³/48)ΦK6(u)`.
The threshold equation `Φ_{un}(n) = 1` with `Phi_fourth_order` gives
`F(L+δ) = uΦS(u)/(2n) + D(u)/n² + E(u)/n³ + O(n^{-4})`, `F(u) = 1 − 1/(e^u−1)`, and
substituting `δ = a₁/n + a₂/n² + a₃/n³` yields the exact coefficients

| coefficient | closed form | value |
|---|---|---|
| `a₁` | `3L/2` | `1.0397207708…` |
| `a₂` | `3L² − (25/12)L` | `−0.002697584411948…` (= the known OP-5 `c`) |
| `a₃` | `(73L − 244L² + 200L³)/8` | `−0.003232602172406…` (**new**) |

Two independent derivations agree ([`lib/op56_fourth.py`](lib/op56_fourth.py): moment
route and exact-`e^{-u}` closed-form route), and 60-digit Newton solutions of
`Φ_{un}(n)=1` for `n = 10^4,10^5,10^6` give `n³(u − L − a₁/n − a₂/n²) → a₃`, with
Richardson extrapolation matching `a₃` to `3·10⁻¹⁵`.

**Note on the Lean arithmetic style.** The remaining arithmetic goals in the headline
assembly were closed following [`linarith-agent-prompt.md`](research/twin-prime-parity/linarith-agent-prompt.md)
(committed `linarith only [ … ]` lists on cleaned goals, named sign facts, no retry
ladder). Two `set_option maxHeartbeats` directives and some bare `linarith`/`nlinarith`
calls remain in the pre-existing body of `PhiFifth.lean`; removing them requires
restructuring eight tactics that time out at the default budget, and is recorded as
follow-up polish rather than silently left unmentioned. The build is green, `sorry`-free
and `axiom`-free.

### 5.1 The `rh40` round-01 `p(L)` attack — `OP-34`, `OP-35`, `OP-36`, `OP-37`

Full report: [`research/attacks/OP-34-36-37-35.md`](research/attacks/OP-34-36-37-35.md);
helpers [`lib/tpp_window_collision.py`](lib/tpp_window_collision.py) (self-test 7/7, exit 0,
re-run here) and [`research/attacks/validate_op34.py`](research/attacks/validate_op34.py).

* **OP-34 + OP-36 — the `[DREAM]` class sum is REFUTED, the exact criterion is PROVED.**
  The "sum over `(i,j)` classes of their window counts" over-counts `p(L)` on exactly
  **604/1399** `L` for `x = 1/π`; the source's literal
  `1 + #{} + Σ_{i≤j}T(i,j)` over-counts on **all 1399** (`T(i,j)` counts last-index `≤ j`,
  so each window is counted `m−J+1` times). Cause: the classes are **not disjoint** — the
  same 604 `L`. The corrected criterion is
  `factor(t) = factor(t') ⟺ x(t) = x(t') ∧ shape(t) = shape(t')` with
  `x = a_i − t`, `shape = (0, a_{i+1}−a_i, …, a_j−a_i)`, and the corrected exact formula
  `p(L) = [∃ all-zero] + Σ_shapes |⋃_{C: shape} X(C)|` — group by **gap-run shape** and take
  the **union** of offset intervals `X(i,j)` (given in the report). Validated on
  **6 378 064** exhaustive cases (`m+1 ≤ 4`, `N ≤ 31`), 1 248 945 class pairs, plus every
  `L` of `1/π`, `log 2`, `N = 13000`, `√2−1`, `e−2`: **0 mismatches**.
* **OP-37(a) realisability — PROVED.** Realised `(i,x)` is exactly
  `max(0, a_i − (N−L)) ≤ x ≤ min(d_{i−1}−1, a_i, L−1)`; the survey's 95 826/0 reproduced.
* **OP-37(b) all-zero — source REFUTED, corrected form PROVED.** Witness `((0,4), N=6, L=3)`
  (independently reproduced here: an all-zero window exists but the source criterion says
  not). The correct criterion is `L ≤ max(a_0, max_j(d_j−1), N−1−a_m)` — the source is wrong
  on 24 337/95 826 cases, the corrected form on 0.
* **OP-37(c) injectivity — source REFUTED, corrected form PROVED (stronger than surveyed).**
  Witness `((12,20), N=26, L=12)` (reproduced: `(0,7),(1,7)` share the factor `(7,)`).
  Corrected: `p(L) ≥ a_m + 2 ⟹` the window→factor map is injective, **with no `N`
  hypothesis** (proof: every nonempty window starts at `t ≤ a_m`, so there are at most
  `a_m+1` of them; a collision forces `p ≤ a_m+1`). Machine-checked as
  `Rh40.injOn_of_card_ge` in
  [`rounds/rh40/lean/Rh40/Plateau.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/rounds/rh40/lean/Rh40/Plateau.lean);
  `./check.sh --all` **2/2 green, exit 0** (re-run here: `Plateau.lean` 37 s, root 21 s).
  Checked on 463 771 plateau / 704 632 conditional / 15 087 survey-loop cases, 0 violations.
* **OP-35 — REFUTED / undefined.** `S_{1,k}` is **undefined corpus-wide** (two prose
  mentions; the `d_j` indexing is also unfixed). The natural reading `S_{1,k} = Σ_{i≤k} d_i`
  gives `D(L) = (L−12)_+` for `1/π`, switching on at `L = 13`, whereas the measured `2→1`
  slope drop is at `L = 14` (`p(13)=16, p(14)=18, p(15)=19`). No partial-sum convention
  repairs it (it would need `S_{1,−1} = 1`), and the natural `D` is unbounded while a
  cancelled-pair deficit must be bounded.

*Honest caveat (from the attack):* the injectivity theorem is stated conditionally on
`p(L) ≥ a_m + 2`; the harvested plateau *value* `max p = a_m + 2` is still unproved and is
used only to instantiate it.

### 5.2 The residual-orbit attack — `OP-28`, `OP-30`, `OP-33`

Full report: [`research/attacks/OP-28-30-33.md`](research/attacks/OP-28-30-33.md); helper
[`lib/tpp_no_limit_orbit.py`](lib/tpp_no_limit_orbit.py) (self-test 5/5, exit 0, re-run
here); compute script [`research/attacks/op28_30_33_compute.py`](research/attacks/op28_30_33_compute.py).

* **OP-28 ≡ OP-30 — the no-limit family is PROVED (constructive).** There exist `x ∈ (0,1)`
  and a greedy orbit with `limsup_K (1/K)Σ_{k<K} log c_k ≥ −0.76` and `liminf_K ≤ −1.21`,
  so the running mean has **no limit**. Construction: prescribe `α_k` alternating `1/2, 1/4`
  in blocks `M_j = 3^j` (exact target `α_k = (q_k²+2q_k)/q_{k+1}`), build `q_k` **backwards**
  by the exact inverse `u_k = n_k u_{k+1}/(n_k + u_{k+1})` (`n_k = q_k+2`, `u = 1/r`), and
  take `x = Σ_{k≥1} 1/(q_k+2)`. Rigour: each backward bracket lies inside its digit cell
  `(q_k+1, q_k+2]` (verified exactly), the backward map is a contraction with
  `|s_k − α_k| ≤ η_k` and `Ση_k ≤ 1.6·10⁻³` (exact-rational recursion), and the block-end
  running means of `log α_k` form an exact 2-cycle with gap `0.35–0.52 ≫ 10⁻³`. Exact
  witness `x = 300129656263973531720568953662090234 / 48845289055200132283765298144075427525`
  realises `q_1..q_4`. *(The survey's squaring law and `q_{k+1} = ⌊q_k²/α_k⌋` were re-derived:
  both correct, the latter to leading order only; the exact self-consistent target is the
  `α_k` above.)*
* **OP-33(a) — the precision floor is PROVED, and closed in Lean here.** If `r` is
  nonnegative, `r_0 ≤ 1/10`, `r_{k+1} ≤ r_k²`, and `10^{−D} < r_{K−1}`, then `2^{K−1} ≤ D`
  — a forward orbit at `D` decimal digits can run only `K ≤ log₂ D + 1` steps. The attack
  left this as a non-compiling WIP file; it is now landed and axiom-clean as
  `Rh42.step_bound` in
  [`rounds/rh42/lean/Rh42/PrecisionFloor.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/rounds/rh42/lean/Rh42/PrecisionFloor.lean),
  wired into `check.sh --all` and `Rh42.lean` (`./check.sh --all` **5/5 green, exit 0**),
  `#print axioms` = `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`. The source's
  "7–13 steps before underflow" (measured `D = 50…3000 → 6…12`) is therefore a **theorem,
  not a bug**.
* **OP-33(b) — EVIDENCE.** Means of `log c_k` over `10⁴` prescribed (backward-realised)
  steps converge to the mean of `log α_k`: `−0.6931` (`1/2`), `−1.3863` (`1/4`), `−2.3026`
  (`1/10`), `−0.7557` (the survey's `10^j` blocks). **None is `−1`**; the source's claim is
  confirmed but re-attributed — no universal limit exists, and the finite-`K` mean is
  strictly below the `s`-mean by the un-decayed gap `Γ_K/K`, so at `K ≤ 15` no convergence
  can be read off.

**The gap.** `Rh45.archimedean_deriv_bound_of_digamma_series` took as its only
hypothesis the Euler–Maclaurin/Hurwitz series
`ψ^{(k)}(z) = (−1)^{k+1} k! Σ_{j≥0}(z+j)^{−k−1}`, hence
`‖ψ^{(k)}(1/4+it/2)‖ ≤ k! Σ_j (1/4+j)^{−k−1}`. Mathlib's `Complex.digamma` carried
only the recurrence/reflection/duplication identities.

**Two new modules.**

* [`Rh45/GammaProduct.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/010/lean/Rh45/GammaProduct.lean)
  (the crux). Mathlib has the complex Gauss product **pointwise**
  (`Complex.GammaSeq`, `Complex.GammaSeq_tendsto_Gamma`) but no locally uniform
  version, hence no way to differentiate the limit. The module proves
  `analyticAt_GammaSeq`, the uniform bound `‖GammaSeq s n‖ ≤ Γ(re s)` (via the integral
  representation, *not* the crude `n^s n!/∏` bound — the latter is not uniform on a
  circle), **`tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn_GammaSeq`** (`GammaSeq · n → Γ` locally uniformly
  on `re s > 0`), then `tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn_deriv_GammaSeq`,
  `tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn_logDeriv_GammaSeq` (Weierstrass differentiation,
  `TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn.deriv`), and the finite identity
  `logDeriv (GammaSeq · n) s = log n − Σ_{j≤n}(s+j)⁻¹`. The local-uniform step is by the
  **circle-Cauchy route**: Cauchy's formula on `C(c,ρ)` bounds the discrepancy by
  `(2π)⁻¹ρ(ρ−r)⁻¹·A_n` with the *scalar* `A_n = ∫θ ‖GammaSeq·n − Γ‖(circleMap c ρ θ)`,
  and `A_n → 0` by dominated convergence on a finite-measure interval — so no
  Vitali/Montel theorem is needed. A companion note
  [`Rh45/GAMMA_PRODUCT.md`](research/twin-prime-parity/010/lean/Rh45/GAMMA_PRODUCT.md)
  records it. (Mathlib's own docstring at `BohrMollerup.lean:29` points to
  `Complex.Gamma_seq_tendsto_Gamma`, a name that does not exist; the real object is
  `Complex.GammaSeq` in `Beta.lean`.)
* [`Rh45/PolygammaSeries.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/010/lean/Rh45/PolygammaSeries.lean).
  The explicit iterated derivative `iteratedDeriv_logDeriv_GammaSeq`
  (`deriv^[k](logDeriv (GammaSeq·n)) s = (−1)^{k+1} k! Σ_{j≤n}(s+j)^{−k−1}` for `k ≥ 1`),
  the **Gauss/Hurwitz series** `digamma_polygamma_series` (`HasSum`), summability
  `summable_polygamma_series`, the norm bound
  `norm_deriv_digamma_le : ‖ψ^{(k)}(s)‖ ≤ k! Σ_j (re s + j)^{−k−1}`, the specialisation
  `Rh45.digamma_series_bound` at `s = 1/4 + it/2`, and the **unconditional**
  `Rh45.archimedean_deriv_bound (k) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (t) : ‖Ψ^{(k)}(t)‖ ≤ psiSeriesBound k`.
  The conditional `archimedean_deriv_bound_of_digamma_series` is kept for compatibility.

**The `k = 0` case, handled honestly.** `Σ_j (1/4+j)^{−1}` diverges, so
`psiSeriesBound 0 = 0` (`Rh45.psiSeriesBound_zero`) and the `k = 0` instance of the
conditional theorem carries no information. A *valid* crude `k = 0` bound is supplied
instead, `Rh45.norm_digamma_le`, from the Weierstrass partial-sum form
`ψ(s) = −γ + Σ_j(1/(j+1) − (s+j)⁻¹)` plus `Real.tendsto_harmonic_sub_log`.

**Paper.** The whole bridge is written up as
[`research/twin-prime-parity/010/polygamma.html`](research/twin-prime-parity/010/polygamma.html)
(*The polygamma series, proved*), in the round's standard HTML style: abstract, contents,
the problem, definitions, the Mathlib inventory, the locally uniform Gauss product (with the
circle-Cauchy inequality and the scalar dominated-convergence argument), Weierstrass
differentiation, the polygamma series, the norm bound and the unconditional archimedean budget,
the `k = 0` diagnosis and replacement bound, a status table, and reproduction/references. It is
linked from `010/index.html` and from `010/lean/README.md`.

**Primer.** The three certification strategies are written up for a reader new to the
material as [`research/twin-prime-parity/010/routes-abc-primer.html`](research/twin-prime-parity/010/routes-abc-primer.html)
(*Routes A, B, C — a pedagogical guide*): what certifying a zero means, the Riemann–Siegel
`Z` dictionary, the three failure modes of naive computation, Route A (IVT + strict monotonicity +
simplicity, in enclosure form, with the `γ₁…γ₅` certificates), Route B (Turing's cardinality squeeze,
the rectangle/half-path `I₃` geometry, `N(T) = Im(I₃)/π`, and the three hypotheses — `hAP`, the
winding number, ξ reality/entireness — that are now theorems), Route C (the explicit-formula split,
Chebyshev prime tail, Simpson archimedean tail, the `9.08·10⁻⁹ ≤ 2.79·10⁻⁸` result), a
proved/certified/cited ledger, and the honest statement that RH is not addressed. Four SVG figures
generated by `lib/routes_figs.py`. Linked from `010/index.html`.

**Net effect on the round.** The archimedean derivative budget `‖Ψ^{(k)}(t)‖ ≤
psiSeriesBound k` is now a theorem for every `k ≥ 1` (`k = 1,…,4` are exactly the cases
the composite-Simpson assembly uses), and the `k = 0` slot has an explicit finite bound.
No hypothesis of `Archimedean.lean` remains unproved except the one that was previously
named and is now discharged; the full `Rh45` development is self-contained.

## 9. Can Routes A, B, C be generalised? (round `011`, 2026-10-12)

**Answer: the theorem cores already are.** A new folder
[`research/twin-prime-parity/011/`](research/twin-prime-parity/011) audits the 010 routes against
four readings of "generalise" and finds that the first reading is already satisfied, because the 010
theorems were written at the right level:

* `exists_unique_root_of_sign_change` is `∀ f : ℝ → ℝ` — no arithmetic at all;
* `turing_reduction` is `∀ Finset α`, `α` arbitrary — pure combinatorics;
* `routeB_reduction_general` is `∀ f : ℂ → ℂ`, with only *analyticity on the rectangle*, a
  *functional equation* `f(1−s) = f(s)`, *conjugation reality* `f(conj s) = conj(f s)`, and zero data
  — `ζ` never appears in a hypothesis;
* `validated_truncation_bound` is a triangle inequality for any decomposition (generalised here to
  `n` tails).

So the work is **instantiation**, not new mathematics: per object one supplies an interval evaluator
(Route A/C), a functional equation and reality (Route B), and an explicit formula (Route C).

**The refined finding (this is the interesting part).** Route B does *not* actually need the bare
self-duality `F(1−s) = F(s)`; it needs only the reflection `logDeriv F (1−s) = −logDeriv F(s)`, and that
survives `h(1−s) = ε·h(s)` for **every** nonzero `ε` — differentiating gives `−h′(1−s) = ε h′(s)`, and
the `ε` cancels in the quotient. The bare identity is *not* recoverable when `ε ≠ 1` (no constant
rescaling helps, since `logDeriv (c·F) = logDeriv F`). Consequently the **root number is not an
obstruction** to Route B, only to the cosmetic rewriting `F(1−s) = F(s)`. The Lean encodes both
interfaces: `SelfDualReal` and the more general `SelfDualRealUpToSign` /
`routeB_general_of_logDeriv`, with `logDeriv_one_sub_of_const_mul` proving the `ε`-cancellation.

**Concrete instantiation: Dirichlet `L`-functions.** Mathlib has `completedLFunction`,
`rootNumber`, `differentiableAt_completedLFunction` and the functional equation
`IsPrimitive.completedLFunction_one_sub`
(`Λ(1−s) = N^{s−1/2}·rootNumber χ·Λ_{χ⁻¹}(s)`). Round 011 **proves the normalisation**
`dirichletL_normalised_one_sub`: with `χ⁻¹ = χ` (real/quadratic character) the function
`h(s) = N^{s/2}Λ_χ(s)` satisfies `h(1−s) = rootNumber χ · h(s)` — the exponent bookkeeping being
`(1−s)/2 + (s−½) = s/2`. Via the `ε`-cancellation this delivers Route B's hypothesis. What remains is
**one substantive Mathlib gap** — conjugation reality
`∀ s, Λ_χ(conj s) = conj(Λ_χ s)` for real `χ`, absent from the `LSeries` files, though 010's proved
`completedRiemannZeta₀_conj` is a transcription template — plus a *proof-technical* `ε ∈ {±1}` case
split in the landed `routeB_for_dirichletL` (not mathematically necessary, per the paragraph above),
and of course an interval engine for a Dirichlet `L`, which does not exist.

**What cannot generalise.** (i) Any all-zeros conclusion: the hypotheses are finitely many enclosures,
so the routes certify finite windows; the all-zeros statement for an `L`-function is (G)RH. (ii) The
interval engine: `010/rigorous/` is engineered around `ζ`'s Dirichlet series and its singularity
structure. (iii) Route A's simplicity conclusion (a `k`-th order certificate is a genuine extension).
(iv) The archimedean budget outside the `Γ` family.

**Artifacts.** `011/README.md`; `011/index.html` (the paper, with two figures);
`011/notes/generalisation-analysis.md` (prose audit) and `011/notes/generality-lean.md` (Lean
inventory); `011/lean/Generic.lean` (namespace `RouteABC`: `SelfDualReal`, `routeB_of_selfDualReal`,
`SelfDualRealUpToSign`, `routeB_general_of_logDeriv`, `logDeriv_one_sub_of_const_mul`,
`CertifiedZero.exists_unique_root`, `validated_truncation_bound_finset`/`_three`,
`dirichletL_normalised_one_sub`, `dirichletCompleted_selfDual`, `dirichletCompleted_conj`,
`RootNumberSign`, `CompletedLFunctionConj`, `routeB_for_dirichletL`) plus `Axioms.lean`;
`011/verify/check_claims.py` (5 independent checks, `ALL CHECKS PASSED`); figures generated by
`lib/generality_figs.py`. Build `011/lean/check.sh --all` is **green**, and all eleven headline
theorems have footprint `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

| `[0, 3π/2)` | `−117754` | `118876` | `1.1775·10⁻⁵` | `1.1888` | `0.5067 ± 0.0133` |

**Reading.** All three arcs sit on the square-root branch (`α ≈ 1/2`) and `|C_I|/x`
falls by another order of magnitude from `10^9`, so the data remain consistent with
`C_I(x) = o(x)` — i.e. **for** P1, not against it. No arc shows `|C_I|/x` bounded below,
so there is no finite-range refutation. This is a description on `[1,10^{10}]`, **not**
an asymptotic claim, and it proves nothing: `P1`/`P2` stay OPEN. Sanity numbers remain
correct (`Σλ(10^{10})/x = −1.16·10⁻⁵`, `#{λ=1}/x = 0.499994`, twisted sums `≤ 1.25·10⁻⁵`).
No zero defect anywhere.

### 3.5 J5 — xi-horn citations verified

**Status: `[x]` done.** The two outstanding `[ ]` items of `xi-horn/TODO.md` **A1** are

**Gentili–Struppa 2007.** *G. Gentili, D. C. Struppa, "A new theory of regular functions
of a quaternionic variable," Adv. Math. **216**(1) (2007) 279–301,
doi:[10.1016/j.aim.2007.05.010](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aim.2007.05.010).*
Title, authors and venue confirmed (the paper is cited as [1] by the follow-up and
indexed as Zbl 1124.30015); the Elsevier DOI resolves (paywalled). **The Representation
Formula quoted in [`xi-horn/CONTINUATION.md`](xi-horn/CONTINUATION.md) §8.1 as (26) is
correct**: the standard statement ([Colombo–Gentili–Sabadini–Struppa,
arXiv:0905.1861](https://arxiv.org/abs/0905.1861), *Extension results for slice regular
functions*, Thm 3.1, attributing it to Gentili–Struppa 2007 and to [5]) is
`f(x+yI) = ½[f(x+yJ) + f(x−yJ)] + I·½[J[f(x−yJ) − f(x+yJ)]]`, which expands to
`½[(1 − IJ) f(x+yJ) + (1 + IJ) f(x−yJ)]` — exactly (26). So the §8.1 argument that a
slice-regular function carries "exactly the information of a holomorphic function of one
complex variable" rests on a correctly quoted theorem.

**Connes.** *A. Connes, "Trace formula in noncommutative geometry and the zeros of the
Riemann zeta function," Selecta Math. **5** (1999), no. 1, 29–106* — the full
bibliographic data is **confirmed verbatim in the abstract of Connes–Consani** below
("Selecta Math. 5 (1999), no. 1, 29--106"). The three pulled papers are confirmed:

|---|---|---|
| Connes–Moscovici, *Prolate spheroidal operator and Zeta* | [2112.05500](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.05500) | **confirmed** — submitted 10 Dec 2021, 17 pp.; abstract: the restriction of `W` to the complement of `J` has negative eigenvalues whose ultraviolet behaviour reproduces the squares of the zeta zeros, with eigenfunctions in the Sonin space, fitting the proof of Weil positivity at the archimedean place |
| Connes–Consani, *Weil positivity and Trace formula, the archimedean place* | [2006.13771](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.13771) | **confirmed** — submitted 24 Jun 2020, 57 pp.; abstract cites the 1999 Selecta paper and states that "Weil positivity implies RH" in the general semi-local case |

### 3.6 J9 — sign-blindness / the parity principle formalised (O12)

**Status: `[x]` done.** New Lean module
[`Rh47/Parity.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/rounds/rh47/lean/Rh47/Parity.lean)
(268 lines, added to `Rh47/lean/check.sh --all` and to `Rh47.lean`; `./check.sh --all`
is **3/3 green**, `Rh47/Sparse.lean` 5 s, `Rh47/Parity.lean` 31 s, root 26 s). The
programme's O12 asked for a Lean statement of the parity principle "in the restricted
setting of weight families generated by small-prime residue conditions"; that family is
now *defined*, and the principle is a *theorem* in it.

**The family.** `sieveWeight D c n = ∑_{d∈D} c d · 1_{d∣n}` — the **sign-blind
linear-sieve weights**: fixed by finitely many divisibility conditions, with no
reference to `λ` or `Ω`.

**Theorems (all `#print axioms` = `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).**

| theorem | statement |
|---|---|
| `sieveLam_collapse` | `∑_{n≤N} w(n)λ(n) = ∑_{d∈D} c_d λ(d) · (∑_{m≤N/d} λ(m))` — the exact **parity collapse**: every sign-blind weight sees `λ` only through the one-point sums |
| `sieveLam_abs_le` | if the one-point sums are `≤ ε·M` for all `M ≤ N` then `\|∑_{n≤N} w(n)λ(n)\| ≤ (∑_d \|c_d\|)·ε·N` — the sieve multiplies the available decay, it cannot create its own |
| `sieveLam_vanishes` | **the parity principle**: if `∑_{m≤M} λ(m) = o(M)` (PNT = `k = 1` Chowla, carried as the explicit hypothesis `LiouvilleVanishes`), then **every** sign-blind weight has `∑_{n≤N} w(n)λ(n) = o(N)` |
| `corr_twist_two` | `∑_{n≤N} (λ(n)(−1)^n)(λ(n+2)(−1)^{n+2}) = ∑_{n≤N} λ(n)λ(n+2)` — the index-parity twist cancels identically (rh47's `0/10⁶`-mismatch identity, now proved) |

The collapse was cross-checked numerically on `1/π`-independent small cases
(`D = {2,3}`, `c = (5,−2)`, `N = 10, 37, 100`: both sides agree). **Honest reading:** this
formalises the *algebraic skeleton* of Selberg's parity obstruction — a bounded-depth
linear sieve cannot manufacture a `λ`-correlation — not the full quantitative
sieve-level statement; the `k = 1` Chowla/PNT input stays a hypothesis, exactly as
register item OP-2 (settled) and O13 (J6, deferred) record.

### 3.8 J8 — the rectangle argument principle for Route B / T8

**Status: `[x]` done.** New Lean module
[`Rh45/ArgumentPrinciple.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/010/lean/Rh45/ArgumentPrinciple.lean)
(added to `010/lean/check.sh --all` and to `Rh45.lean`; docs in
[`Rh45/ARGUMENT_PRINCIPLE.md`](research/twin-prime-parity/010/lean/Rh45/ARGUMENT_PRINCIPLE.md)).
Independently re-run here: **`./check.sh --all` 7/7 `[check] OK`, exit 0**
(`ArgumentPrinciple.lean` 25 s), `#print axioms` on the six headline theorems =
`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

**What was built.** The whole contour computation for `∮_{∂R}(s−a)^{-1} ds`, by hand,
with no homotopy/winding-number API: `Complex.log` antiderivatives on each of the four
edges (`integral_inv_horizontal`, `integral_inv_vertical_right`, `integral_inv_vertical_left`),
the two slit-plane `arg` jumps (`log_sub_log_neg`, `log_neg_sub_log`), and then

| theorem | statement |
|---|---|
| `rectBoundary_inv_of_mem` | `a` strictly inside `[0,1]×[t₀,t₁]` ⟹ `∮ (s−a)^{-1} = 2πi` |
| `rectBoundary_inv_of_notMem` | `a` outside the closed rectangle ⟹ `∮ (s−a)^{-1} = 0` |
| `logDeriv_prod_pow` | `logDeriv (C·∏(s−z)^{m z}) = ∑ m z·(s−z)^{-1}` |
| `argument_principle_factorized` | under a local factorisation `f =ᶠ C·∏(s−z)^{m z}` with all `z` strictly inside: `∮_{∂R} f'/f = 2πi·∑ m z` |
| `routeB_reduction_factorized` | discharges the former `hAP` hypothesis: `(rightPath (logDeriv f) t₀ t₁).im = π·∑ m z` |

The key technical device is that the left edge `Re s = 0` crosses the branch slit, so the
*shifted* antiderivative `log(a − iy)` (whose real part is `a.re > 0`) is used; with
`u₀ = a − it₀` (`Im > 0`), `u₁ = a − it₁` (`Im < 0`) the four edge values telescope to
`iπ + iπ = 2πi`.

**Follow-up landed after the first pass: the Weierstrass step.** New module
[`Rh45/Weierstrass.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/010/lean/Rh45/Weierstrass.lean)
(536 lines, added to `010/lean/check.sh --all`; docs in
[`Rh45/WEIERSTRASS.md`](research/twin-prime-parity/010/lean/Rh45/WEIERSTRASS.md);
re-run here: **8/8 `[check] OK`, exit 0**, `#print axioms` on the four headline theorems =
`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, no `sorry`/`axiom`/`maxHeartbeats`, all
arithmetic as committed `linarith only […]` lists). **Route B now uses it:** a further
module [`Rh45/RouteBGeneral.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/010/lean/Rh45/RouteBGeneral.lean)
proves `routeB_reduction_general`,
`(rightPath (logDeriv f) t₀ t₁).im = π·∑_{z∈Z} m z`, from analyticity of `f`, its zero data
on the rectangle, and the two structural identities alone — no factorisation hypothesis and
no constant `C`. `routeB_reduction_factorized` is kept for compatibility and marked
superseded; `010/lean/check.sh --all` is now **9/9 green** and `routeB_reduction_general` is
axiom-clean. It supplies exactly the ingredient the first pass had named as missing:

| theorem | statement |
|---|---|
| `exists_factorization` | if `f` is analytic on a neighbourhood of the closed rectangle and its only zeros there are the points of a finite `Z` (interior, orders `m`), then `f = g · ∏_{z∈Z}(s−z)^{m z}` with `g` analytic **and nowhere zero** on the closed rectangle |
| `rectBoundary_logDeriv_eq_zero` | `g` analytic and nonvanishing there ⟹ `∮_{∂R} g′/g = 0` (Cauchy–Goursat for the rectangle, via `Complex.integral_boundary_rect_eq_zero_of_differentiableOn` at `z = t₀i`, `w = 1 + t₁i`) |
| `argument_principle_of_factorization` | the argument principle from an explicit zero-free factor `g` |
| `argument_principle_general` | `∮_{∂R} f′/f = 2πi·Σ_{z∈Z} m z` **with no factorisation hypothesis** — `exists_factorization` is applied inside |

**How the factorisation is built.** At each `z ∈ Z` the order is finite (otherwise `f`
would vanish on a punctured neighbourhood, contradicting the no-other-zeros hypothesis), so
Mathlib's local order factorisation `AnalyticAt.analyticOrderAt_ne_top` gives `h z` analytic
at `z` with `h z z ≠ 0` and `f =ᶠ[𝓝 z] (·−z)^{m z}·h z`. The glued factor is
`g s := if s ∈ Z then h s s / ∏_{z'≠s}(s−z')^{m z'} else f s / ∏_{z'∈Z}(s−z')^{m z'}`;
analyticity and nonvanishing are checked pointwise (at `z ∈ Z` via the eventual identity
`g =ᶠ h z/∏_{z'≠z}(·−z')^{m z'}`), and the product identity holds because both sides are
eventually equal at each zero and analytic. The argument principle then separates
`logDeriv f = logDeriv g + Σ m z/(·−z)` (product rule, `logDeriv_prod_pow`), kills the first
term by the Cauchy–Goursat lemma, and evaluates the second by the already-proved
`rectBoundary_inv_of_mem` (= `2πi`).

**What is *still* not claimed.** The zero set is still an input (`Z : Finset` plus "no other
zeros"), not derived from analyticity + compactness; the instance `f = ξ` additionally needs
an analytic `xi` on the rectangle (the `RouteBAnalytic` `xi` has removable singularities at
`0,1`), the reality `ξ(conj s) = conj(ξ s)`, and the zero-set identification — all
pre-existing gaps, not argument-principle or factorisation issues. No statement is made for
zeros on `∂R`. One hypothesis is genuinely needed and is made explicit in
`argument_principle_of_factorization`: analyticity of `f` on the rectangle, because
`logDeriv f` involves `deriv f`, a germ condition that pointwise `f = g·P` on the closed
rectangle does not determine (the requested literal signature without it is false — modify
`f` smoothly outside the rectangle).

### 3.9 J7 — the threshold-form fourth-order expansion

**Status: `[x]` done.** New Lean module
[`Op56/PhiFifth.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/open/lean/Op56/PhiFifth.lean) (added to
`open/lean/check.sh --all` and to `Op56.lean`). Independently re-run here:
**`./check.sh --all` 10/10 `[check] OK`, exit 0** (`PhiFifth.lean` 230 s, the rest
~200 s total), and `#print axioms Op56.threshold_fourth_order_uniform` =
`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

**Landed (all proved).** The cubic exponential remainder `exp_sub_three_bound`; the
third-order Taylor expansion `PhiS_taylor3_at_log2`
(`ΦS(u) = 6 − 26δ + 75δ² − (541/3)δ³ + O(δ⁴)`, `δ = u − log 2`); the reusable moment
identity `tsum_quad_poly_log2`; the cubic expansion `uPhiS_expansion_fourth`; the
`D`/`SFourth` definitions; the general first-order moment expansion
`tsum_pow_exp_first_order` / `PhiK_diff_linear_le`; `D_first_order` (exact
`D′(L) = −26/3 + (175/2)L − (541/4)L²`); `EFourth_diff_le`; the model lemmas
`SFourth_model`, `tM_lipschitz`, `tg_lipschitz_wide`, `log_thh_bound`; and the headline

```lean
theorem threshold_fourth_order_uniform :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop, ∀ u : ℝ, 1/2 ≤ u → u ≤ 1 →
      IsThreshold n (u*(n:ℝ)) →
        |u - Real.log 2 - 3*Real.log 2/(2*(n:ℝ))
            - (3*Real.log 2^2 - (25/12)*Real.log 2)/(n:ℝ)^2
            - ((73*Real.log 2 - 244*Real.log 2^2 + 200*Real.log 2^3)/8)/(n:ℝ)^3|
          ≤ C/(n:ℝ)^4
```

**The mathematics (exact, two routes, numerically confirmed).** Let `L = log 2`,
`δ = u − L`, `ΦS(u) = Σ_k k²e^{-uk}`, `ΦKp(u) = Σ_k k^p e^{-uk}`,
`D(u) = −(u/3)ΦK3(u) + (u²/8)ΦK4(u)`, `EFourth(u) = (u/4)ΦK4(u) − (u²/6)ΦK5(u) + (u³/48)ΦK6(u)`.
The threshold equation `Φ_{un}(n) = 1` with `Phi_fourth_order` gives
`F(L+δ) = uΦS(u)/(2n) + D(u)/n² + E(u)/n³ + O(n^{-4})`, `F(u) = 1 − 1/(e^u−1)`, and
substituting `δ = a₁/n + a₂/n² + a₃/n³` yields the exact coefficients

| coefficient | closed form | value |
|---|---|---|
| `a₁` | `3L/2` | `1.0397207708…` |
| `a₂` | `3L² − (25/12)L` | `−0.002697584411948…` (= the known OP-5 `c`) |
| `a₃` | `(73L − 244L² + 200L³)/8` | `−0.003232602172406…` (**new**) |

Two independent derivations agree ([`lib/op56_fourth.py`](lib/op56_fourth.py): moment
route and exact-`e^{-u}` closed-form route), and 60-digit Newton solutions of
`Φ_{un}(n)=1` for `n = 10^4,10^5,10^6` give `n³(u − L − a₁/n − a₂/n²) → a₃`, with
Richardson extrapolation matching `a₃` to `3·10⁻¹⁵`.

**Note on the Lean arithmetic style.** The remaining arithmetic goals in the headline
assembly were closed following [`linarith-agent-prompt.md`](research/twin-prime-parity/linarith-agent-prompt.md)
(committed `linarith only [ … ]` lists on cleaned goals, named sign facts, no retry
ladder). Two `set_option maxHeartbeats` directives and some bare `linarith`/`nlinarith`
calls remain in the pre-existing body of `PhiFifth.lean`; removing them requires
restructuring eight tactics that time out at the default budget, and is recorded as
follow-up polish rather than silently left unmentioned. The build is green, `sorry`-free
and `axiom`-free.

### 5.1 The `rh40` round-01 `p(L)` attack — `OP-34`, `OP-35`, `OP-36`, `OP-37`

Full report: [`research/attacks/OP-34-36-37-35.md`](research/attacks/OP-34-36-37-35.md);
helpers [`lib/tpp_window_collision.py`](lib/tpp_window_collision.py) (self-test 7/7, exit 0,
re-run here) and [`research/attacks/validate_op34.py`](research/attacks/validate_op34.py).

* **OP-34 + OP-36 — the `[DREAM]` class sum is REFUTED, the exact criterion is PROVED.**
  The "sum over `(i,j)` classes of their window counts" over-counts `p(L)` on exactly
  **604/1399** `L` for `x = 1/π`; the source's literal
  `1 + #{} + Σ_{i≤j}T(i,j)` over-counts on **all 1399** (`T(i,j)` counts last-index `≤ j`,
  so each window is counted `m−J+1` times). Cause: the classes are **not disjoint** — the
  same 604 `L`. The corrected criterion is
  `factor(t) = factor(t') ⟺ x(t) = x(t') ∧ shape(t) = shape(t')` with
  `x = a_i − t`, `shape = (0, a_{i+1}−a_i, …, a_j−a_i)`, and the corrected exact formula
  `p(L) = [∃ all-zero] + Σ_shapes |⋃_{C: shape} X(C)|` — group by **gap-run shape** and take
  the **union** of offset intervals `X(i,j)` (given in the report). Validated on
  **6 378 064** exhaustive cases (`m+1 ≤ 4`, `N ≤ 31`), 1 248 945 class pairs, plus every
  `L` of `1/π`, `log 2`, `N = 13000`, `√2−1`, `e−2`: **0 mismatches**.
* **OP-37(a) realisability — PROVED.** Realised `(i,x)` is exactly
  `max(0, a_i − (N−L)) ≤ x ≤ min(d_{i−1}−1, a_i, L−1)`; the survey's 95 826/0 reproduced.
* **OP-37(b) all-zero — source REFUTED, corrected form PROVED.** Witness `((0,4), N=6, L=3)`
  (independently reproduced here: an all-zero window exists but the source criterion says
  not). The correct criterion is `L ≤ max(a_0, max_j(d_j−1), N−1−a_m)` — the source is wrong
  on 24 337/95 826 cases, the corrected form on 0.
* **OP-37(c) injectivity — source REFUTED, corrected form PROVED (stronger than surveyed).**
  Witness `((12,20), N=26, L=12)` (reproduced: `(0,7),(1,7)` share the factor `(7,)`).
  Corrected: `p(L) ≥ a_m + 2 ⟹` the window→factor map is injective, **with no `N`
  hypothesis** (proof: every nonempty window starts at `t ≤ a_m`, so there are at most
  `a_m+1` of them; a collision forces `p ≤ a_m+1`). Machine-checked as
  `Rh40.injOn_of_card_ge` in
  [`rounds/rh40/lean/Rh40/Plateau.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/rounds/rh40/lean/Rh40/Plateau.lean);
  `./check.sh --all` **2/2 green, exit 0** (re-run here: `Plateau.lean` 37 s, root 21 s).
  Checked on 463 771 plateau / 704 632 conditional / 15 087 survey-loop cases, 0 violations.
* **OP-35 — REFUTED / undefined.** `S_{1,k}` is **undefined corpus-wide** (two prose
  mentions; the `d_j` indexing is also unfixed). The natural reading `S_{1,k} = Σ_{i≤k} d_i`
  gives `D(L) = (L−12)_+` for `1/π`, switching on at `L = 13`, whereas the measured `2→1`
  slope drop is at `L = 14` (`p(13)=16, p(14)=18, p(15)=19`). No partial-sum convention
  repairs it (it would need `S_{1,−1} = 1`), and the natural `D` is unbounded while a
  cancelled-pair deficit must be bounded.

*Honest caveat (from the attack):* the injectivity theorem is stated conditionally on
`p(L) ≥ a_m + 2`; the harvested plateau *value* `max p = a_m + 2` is still unproved and is
used only to instantiate it.

### 5.2 The residual-orbit attack — `OP-28`, `OP-30`, `OP-33`

Full report: [`research/attacks/OP-28-30-33.md`](research/attacks/OP-28-30-33.md); helper
[`lib/tpp_no_limit_orbit.py`](lib/tpp_no_limit_orbit.py) (self-test 5/5, exit 0, re-run
here); compute script [`research/attacks/op28_30_33_compute.py`](research/attacks/op28_30_33_compute.py).

* **OP-28 ≡ OP-30 — the no-limit family is PROVED (constructive).** There exist `x ∈ (0,1)`
  and a greedy orbit with `limsup_K (1/K)Σ_{k<K} log c_k ≥ −0.76` and `liminf_K ≤ −1.21`,
  so the running mean has **no limit**. Construction: prescribe `α_k` alternating `1/2, 1/4`
  in blocks `M_j = 3^j` (exact target `α_k = (q_k²+2q_k)/q_{k+1}`), build `q_k` **backwards**
  by the exact inverse `u_k = n_k u_{k+1}/(n_k + u_{k+1})` (`n_k = q_k+2`, `u = 1/r`), and
  take `x = Σ_{k≥1} 1/(q_k+2)`. Rigour: each backward bracket lies inside its digit cell
  `(q_k+1, q_k+2]` (verified exactly), the backward map is a contraction with
  `|s_k − α_k| ≤ η_k` and `Ση_k ≤ 1.6·10⁻³` (exact-rational recursion), and the block-end
  running means of `log α_k` form an exact 2-cycle with gap `0.35–0.52 ≫ 10⁻³`. Exact
  witness `x = 300129656263973531720568953662090234 / 48845289055200132283765298144075427525`
  realises `q_1..q_4`. *(The survey's squaring law and `q_{k+1} = ⌊q_k²/α_k⌋` were re-derived:
  both correct, the latter to leading order only; the exact self-consistent target is the
  `α_k` above.)*
* **OP-33(a) — the precision floor is PROVED, and closed in Lean here.** If `r` is
  nonnegative, `r_0 ≤ 1/10`, `r_{k+1} ≤ r_k²`, and `10^{−D} < r_{K−1}`, then `2^{K−1} ≤ D`
  — a forward orbit at `D` decimal digits can run only `K ≤ log₂ D + 1` steps. The attack
  left this as a non-compiling WIP file; it is now landed and axiom-clean as
  `Rh42.step_bound` in
  [`rounds/rh42/lean/Rh42/PrecisionFloor.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/rounds/rh42/lean/Rh42/PrecisionFloor.lean),
  wired into `check.sh --all` and `Rh42.lean` (`./check.sh --all` **5/5 green, exit 0**),
  `#print axioms` = `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`. The source's
  "7–13 steps before underflow" (measured `D = 50…3000 → 6…12`) is therefore a **theorem,
  not a bug**.
* **OP-33(b) — EVIDENCE.** Means of `log c_k` over `10⁴` prescribed (backward-realised)
  steps converge to the mean of `log α_k`: `−0.6931` (`1/2`), `−1.3863` (`1/4`), `−2.3026`
  (`1/10`), `−0.7557` (the survey's `10^j` blocks). **None is `−1`**; the source's claim is
  confirmed but re-attributed — no universal limit exists, and the finite-`K` mean is
  strictly below the `s`-mean by the un-decayed gap `Γ_K/K`, so at `K ≤ 15` no convergence
  can be read off.
