## 50. Density-derived spacing for the zeros (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-0b76cf87`, round 21.

**Proved.** [`011/lean/DirichletZeroCounting.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/011/lean/DirichletZeroCounting.lean):

* `densitySpacing_le_zero` — if the `n`-th zero `γ n` satisfies `γ n ≥ 2` and its index is ≤ the
  cumulative count at `γ n`, then `RiemannVonMangoldtDensity` gives
  `max 0 (√(n/C) − 6) ≤ γ n`, i.e. `γ n ≳ √n`.

This is the **spacing majorant** the zero tail needs: `f n = max 0 (√(n/C) − 6)` is a valid lower
bound for the zero positions, and `Σ h(f n)` converges for any rapidly decaying `h` (e.g. Gaussian
`e^{−t²/2}`).  With it, `zeroTail_le_of_majorant` applies, giving a zero tail conditional only on
the named interface `RiemannVonMangoldtDensity` — the "discharge the density input" clause of
strand (2).

Proof: quadratic count bound (§49) at `T = γ n` gives `n ≤ C(γ n + 6)²`; `√(n/C) ≤ γ n + 6` by
`Real.sqrt_le_iff`; rearrange and take `max` with `0 ≤ γ n`.

**Verification.** `./check.sh --all` green over **25** files; footprint
`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

## 56. Vertical-line transport (Cauchy–Goursat) (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-0b76cf87`, round 27.

**Proved.** [`011/lean/DirichletMellinPrereq.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/011/lean/DirichletMellinPrereq.lean):

* **`verticalLine_transport`** — for `g` continuous on `[1,c]×[t₀,t₁]` and complex-differentiable in
  its interior (`1 ≤ c`):

  `∫_{1}^{c} g(x+it₀) dx − ∫_{1}^{c} g(x+it₁) dx + i·∫_{t₀}^{t₁} g(c+iy) dy
      − i·∫_{t₀}^{t₁} g(1+iy) dy = 0`.

Obtained from Mathlib's rectangle Cauchy–Goursat
(`Complex.integral_boundary_rect_eq_zero_of_differentiable_on_off_countable`), with the
`z.re/z.im` normalization and the `↑1`/`1` coercion reconciled in the `simpa`.

This is the **contour-move tool**: rearranged, it transports the vertical line `Re s = 1` to
`Re s = c > 1` at the cost of the two horizontal edge integrals.  Applying it to
`g = F·Λ_χ'/Λ_χ` (analytic for `Re s > 1`, where `L(s,χ) ≠ 0`) — together with §55's archimedean −
prime decomposition on `Re = c` and the existing zero side — assembles
`archimedean − prime = zero sum`.

**Verification.** `./check.sh --all` green over **25** files; footprint
`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

      = Re(∫_{t₀}^{t₁} F(c+it)·(½log N − ½log π + ½ψ((c+it)/2)) dt)

  with `g = F·Λ_χ'/Λ_χ`.

valid on `Re ≥ c₀ > 1`.  The segment touching `Re = 1` must be handled by a limiting argument.  This

## 64. Analyticity side-conditions discharged (2026-10-13)

**Proved.** [`011/lean/DirichletMellinPrereq.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/011/lean/DirichletMellinPrereq.lean):

* `dirichletCompleted_ne_zero_of_one_lt_re` — `dirichletCompleted χ s ≠ 0` for `Re s > 1`
  (the Euler-product region), from `N^{s/2} ≠ 0` and `completedLFunction_ne_zero_of_one_lt_re`;
* **`continuousOn_mul_logDeriv_dirichletCompleted`** — `F·Λ_χ'/Λ_χ` is continuous on any
  `S ⊆ {Re > 1}` where `F` is continuous (writing `logDeriv = deriv/f`, with `deriv f` continuous

## 80. **BREAKTHROUGH — the strip estimate is proved** (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-0b76cf87`, round 51 (continuation).

Rounds 45, 46, 48 each failed to prove
`norm_logDeriv_dirichletCompleted_le_of_digamma` — the Riemann–von Mangoldt strip estimate
`‖Λ_χ'/Λ_χ(c+it)‖ = O(1 + log(|t|+2))` — with deterministic 200 000-heartbeat timeouts.

**Root cause found: `Complex.digamma` unfolds.**  Mathlib defines `Complex.digamma = logDeriv
Complex.Gamma`, and `Complex.Gamma` is a large definition.  *Every* defeq check whose type mentions
`Complex.digamma …` therefore had to reduce that tower — which is what blew the heartbeat budget,
not the triangle inequality.

**Fix.**  Introduce an opaque wrapper

    @[irreducible] noncomputable def digammaC (z : ℂ) : ℂ := Complex.digamma z

and state `DigammaGrowthBound` in terms of `digammaC`.  With the `irreducible` hint the elaborator
never unfolds it during unification, and the whole proof — `set f := logDeriv (dirichletCompleted χ)`,
`set`-abbreviated constants, `norm_add_le`/`norm_sub_le`, a `ring` key step, and a final `nlinarith` —
elaborates immediately.

**Proved.** [`011/lean/DirichletMellinPrereq.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/011/lean/DirichletMellinPrereq.lean):

* **`norm_logDeriv_dirichletCompleted_le_of_digamma`** — `DigammaGrowthBound χ` implies
  `∃ C > 0, ∀ t, ‖Λ_χ'/Λ_χ(c+it)‖ ≤ C·(1 + log(|t|+2))` for `c > 1`.

This is **the quantitative strip estimate** — the input the Riemann–von Mangoldt count
`N(T+1) − N(T) = O(log qT)` needs, and the barrier that stood for rounds 45–48.

**Verification.** `./check.sh --all` green over **26** files; footprint
`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

  multiplicity-weighted count `∑ m ≤ M/π` (from `dirichletCompleted_routeBCount`:
  `Im(rightPath) = π·∑ m`, and `Im ≤ ‖·‖`);

  then `‖rightPath g t₀ t₁‖ ≤ M·(1 + |t₁ − t₀|)`
  (`intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const` on each segment, `‖i‖ = 1`);

  segments gives

  `∑_{z∈Z} m z ≤ M·(1 + |t₁ − t₀|)/π`.

**This is the argument-principle assembly**: the zero count is now bounded by the contour bound, and

  where `Mh` bounds `g` on the horizontal segments `[1/2, c]` and `Mv` on the vertical edge
  `Re s = c`.

**Why this matters.**  The vertical edge of `rightPath` sits at `Re s = 1`, one unit to the left of
where §80's strip estimate holds.  After the transport the vertical edge is at `Re s = c > 1`,
**where `Mv = C·(1 + log(|t|+2))` is available in closed form** — so the `|t₁ − t₀|·log` term of the
Riemann–von Mangoldt count is now supplied by a proved theorem rather than a hypothesis.  Only the
two horizontal segments `Mh` (through the critical strip `1/2 ≤ Re ≤ 1`) remain.

## 83. Critical-strip interface and the O(log qT) count bound (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-0b76cf87`, round 53.

**Proved.** [`011/lean/DirichletZeroCounting.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/011/lean/DirichletZeroCounting.lean):

* `completedLogDeriv` (`@[irreducible]`, with `completedLogDeriv_def`) — the part-B wrapper applied
  to `logDeriv (dirichletCompleted χ)`;
* **`CriticalStripLogDerivBound χ`** — the named interface
  `∃ C > 0, ∀ σ ∈ [1/2, 2], ∀ t, ‖Λ_χ'/Λ_χ(σ+it)‖ ≤ C·(1 + log(q(|t|+2)))`;
* **`dirichletCompleted_zeroCount_le_of_criticalStrip`** — from that interface, the
  multiplicity-weighted zero count in a rectangle obeys

  `∑_{z∈Z} m z ≤ C·(1 + log(q(T+2)))·(1 + |t₁ − t₀|)/π`

  whenever `|t₀|, |t₁| ≤ T`.

**This is the Riemann–von Mangoldt count bound `N(T+1) − N(T) = O(log qT)`** — for unit height
`|t₁ − t₀| = 1` the right side is `O(log qT)`.  It is derived from §81's assembly plus §80's strip
estimate on the branch `σ > 1`, with the critical-strip range `1/2 ≤ σ ≤ 1` isolated into
`CriticalStripLogDerivBound`.

**Verification.** `./check.sh --all` green over **26** files; footprint
`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

## 84. Multiplicity bridge: `ncard ≤ Σ order` (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-0b76cf87`, round 54.

**Proved.** [`011/lean/DirichletZeroCounting.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/011/lean/DirichletZeroCounting.lean):

* `one_le_analyticOrderNatAt_of_zero` — at an analytic zero whose `analyticOrderAt` is finite, the
  order is at least `1` (`AnalyticAt.analyticOrderAt_eq_zero` + `ENat.toNat_le_toNat`);
* **`ncard_le_sum_analyticOrder`** — for `f` analytic everywhere with finite order at its zeros,
  the number of distinct zeros in a finite set is at most the sum of their orders:
  `S.ncard ≤ ∑_{z ∈ S} analyticOrderNatAt f z`.

This is the bridge from §83's **multiplicity-weighted** count bound to the **distinct-zero** count
used by `RiemannVonMangoldtDensity` (`dirichletZeroCount` is an `ncard`).  With it, the chain

`CriticalStripLogDerivBound` → weighted count `O(log qT)` → `ncard` count `O(log qT)`

is closed except for supplying `analyticAt_dirichletCompleted` and the finiteness of the order at
each zero (which holds because `dirichletCompleted χ` is entire and `χ ≠ 1`, so its zeros are
isolated).

**Verification.** `./check.sh --all` green over **26** files; footprint
`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

## 90. **BREAKTHROUGH — the argument-principle assembly is PROVED** (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-0b76cf87`, round 60.  **§88's decomposition was the answer.**

**The insight.**  Five monolithic attempts (§§85, 87, 88, 89) died because *one* theorem carried the
whole composition: `hbd`, `CriticalStripLogDerivBound`, `dirichletZeroCount`, two
`IntervalIntegrable` locals and the `log` bookkeeping — and the *proof term* then exceeded 1 000 000
heartbeats.  The fix is not a wrapper but **abstraction**:

* **`dirichletZeroCount_le_of_sum_bound`** — a *tiny* theorem, whose statement mentions neither
  `logDeriv` nor the rectangle arithmetic:

  > if `Z ⊇` the zeros in `(T, T+1]`, all elements of `Z` are zeros, and the order sum over `Z` is
  > `≤ B`, then `dirichletZeroCount χ T ≤ B`.

  It is proved by `dirichletZeroCountIn_le_orderSum` (§86) composed with the bound — one line.

* **`dirichletZeroCount_le_of_criticalStrip`** — the consumer, now elaborating in 6 s.  Crucially,
  §83's hypotheses (`Z`, `hno`, `hint₀`, `hint₁`) are passed as **one existential hypothesis** `hZ`
  rather than being derived inline, which keeps the proof term small.

**This is the Riemann–von Mangoldt count bound `N(T+1) − N(T) = O(log(qT))` assembled**, in the form

  `∃ C > 0, dirichletZeroCount χ T ≤ C·(1 + log(q(T+2)))`

from the critical-strip interface, the strip estimate (§80), the transported contour bound (§82), the
argument-principle count (§83) and the multiplicity bridge (§86).

**New module.** `DirichletZeroCount2.lean`, added to `check.sh --all` (now **27 files**), imported by
`AxiomsL.lean`.  Footprint of the assembly:
`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` — no `sorry`, no `axiom`, no `admit`, no `native_decide`,
no `set_option maxHeartbeats`.

**Lesson for the archive.**  When a composition will not elaborate, do not tune the budget and do not
reach for another wrapper: **abstract the composition into a theorem whose statement forgets the
expensive subterms**, then instantiate.  §80's `@[irreducible]` removes reduction from *statements*;
§90's abstraction removes it from *proof terms*.

**Remaining for the objective.**  (i) discharge `CriticalStripLogDerivBound` for `1/2 ≤ σ ≤ 1`;
(ii) supply `hZ` and `htop` unconditionally (boundary-freeness for the compactness argument, and
finiteness of the order at zeros via the identity theorem); (iii) `DigammaGrowthBound` (part C).

  data).

`T ≥ 2`, whereas §94's bound was an `∃ C` *per* `T`.  Two changes made the constant explicit and

2. `RiemannVonMangoldtDensity`'s bound is `C·log(q(T+2))` (no `1 +`), so the `1 + log` was absorbed

## 96. **Correctness fix: `DigammaGrowthBound` was FALSE as stated** (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-0b76cf87`, round 67.  Found while investigating part (C).

**The bug.**  `DigammaGrowthBound` was defined as

  `∃ C > 0, ∀ σ t, 0 < σ → ‖ψ(σ + it)‖ ≤ C·(1 + log(|t| + 2))`

— a **half-plane** statement.  It is **false**: put `t = 0`.  Then the right-hand side is the constant
`C·(1 + log 2)`, while `ψ(σ) ~ log σ → ∞` as `σ → ∞`.  So no such `C` exists.

**Consequence had it stood.**  §80 (`norm_logDeriv_dirichletCompleted_le_of_digamma`) takes
`h : DigammaGrowthBound` as a hypothesis.  A false hypothesis makes the theorem **vacuous**, and the
strip estimate — the foundation of §§81–95 — would have been proved from an unsatisfiable premise.
This is exactly the class of defect the objective's "no `sorry`, no `axiom`" discipline cannot catch:
the proof term is fine, the *statement* is wrong.

**The fix.**  §80 only ever uses the bound at `σ = c/2`, one **fixed vertical line** (the archimedean
term is evaluated at `(c + it)/2` with `c > 1` fixed).  So the definition is now line-based:

  `def DigammaGrowthBound (σ0 : ℝ) : Prop := ∃ C > 0, ∀ t, ‖ψ(σ0 + it)‖ ≤ C·(1 + log(|t| + 2))`

and §80 takes `h : DigammaGrowthBound (c / 2)`.  **This statement is true** — on a fixed vertical
line in `Re > 0` the digamma is `O(log|t|)` (for `|t|` bounded it is bounded on the compact segment;
for `|t| → ∞` the standard asymptotic applies).

**Verification.**  `./check.sh --all` green over **27** files;
`norm_logDeriv_dirichletCompleted_le_of_digamma` still footprint
`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, now from a *satisfiable* hypothesis.

**Lesson.**  When a hypothesis is introduced to name a gap, it must be **checked for satisfiability**
before anything is built on it.  Both remaining interfaces (`CriticalStripLogDerivBound`,
`DigammaGrowthBound (σ0)`) have now been checked for shape; `hbd` is clearly satisfiable *away from
exceptional `T`*, and its boundary analysis is in §95.

## 97. Part (C) reduced to a fixed strip (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-0b76cf87`, round 68.

**Proved.** [`011/lean/DirichletMellinPrereq.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/011/lean/DirichletMellinPrereq.lean):

* **`digammaGrowthBound_of_stripBound`** — a bound
  `‖ψ(σ+it)‖ ≤ C·(1 + log(|t|+2))` valid on the **fixed strip** `1 ≤ σ ≤ 2` implies
  `DigammaGrowthBound σ0` for any `σ0` with `σ0 - n ∈ [1,2]`.

**The argument.**  Mathlib supplies the iterated recurrence
`Complex.digamma_apply_add_nat : ψ(s+n) = ψ(s) + ∑_{k<n} 1/(s+k)`.  Running it backwards,
`ψ(σ0 + it) = ψ((σ0-n) + it) + ∑_{k<n} 1/((σ0-n) + it + k)`.
The shift term is a **finite** sum (`n` is fixed by `σ0`), and since
`|(σ0-n) + it + k| ≥ Re = σ0-n+k ≥ 1`, it is bounded by the constant
`∑_{k<n} 1/(σ0-n+k)` — `O(1)`, uniformly in `t`.  (Contrast: on the whole half-plane the same sum
diverges, which is exactly why §96's original statement was false.)

**Consequence.**  Part (C) is now reduced to a single, sharply stated obligation
(`∃ C, ‖ψ(σ+it)‖ ≤ C(1+log(|t|+2))` on `1 ≤ σ ≤ 2`), which is the digamma asymptotic and needs the
series Mathlib lacks.  This is the *useful* form of the gap: bounded, localised, and true.

**Note on the state of the file.**  An attempt to reorder `def`/`theorem` accidentally duplicated
this section; the duplicate was found and deleted, and the build re-verified.  `./check.sh --all`
green over **27** files; footprint `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

## 98. Part (C): the strip bound is beyond Mathlib's Gamma API (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-0b76cf87`, round 69.  **Investigation, recorded as a finding.**

**Target** (after §97): `∃ C, ∀ σ ∈ [1,2], ∀ t, ‖ψ(σ+it)‖ ≤ C·(1 + log(|t|+2))`.

**What Mathlib has.**  `Complex.digamma` is `logDeriv Gamma`, with exactly:
`digamma_zero`, `digamma_one`, `digamma_one_half`, `digamma_apply_add_one`,
`digamma_apply_add_nat`, `digamma_nat_add_one`, `digamma_one_sub` (reflection),
`meromorphic_digamma`, `digamma_two_mul` (duplication).  **No series, no asymptotic, no bound.**

**Routes checked and closed:**
* **Series** `ψ(z) = −γ + Σ_{k≥0} (1/(k+1) − 1/(z+k))` — not in Mathlib.  Deriving it needs
  `logDeriv` of the Weierstrass product; Mathlib has `GammaSeq` (a convergent sequence) and
  `Gamma_mul_Gamma_one_sub`, but no product/log-derivative limit theorem to build on.
* **Stirling** — `Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Stirling.lean` is **factorial-only**
  (`stirlingSeq`, `factorial_isEquivalent_stirling`).  There is **no complex Stirling asymptotic**
  `log Γ(z) = (z−1/2)log z − z + …`, which is what would give `ψ(z) = log z + O(1/|z|)`.
* **Termwise series bound** — `|term| ≤ |z−1|/(k+1)²` gives only `O(|t|)`, not `O(log|t|)`; the
  `log` bound is intrinsically a *cancellation* phenomenon (Euler–Maclaurin), not termwise.
* **Reflection + recurrence** — the reflection maps `[1,2]` to `[−1,0]` (through the pole at `0`),
  and the recurrence then returns to `[1,2]`; the two give a *relation* among `ψ` values, not a bound.
* **Cauchy estimate** — bounding `ψ = (log Γ)'` from `|log Γ| = O(|t|log|t|)` gives `O(|t|log|t|)`,
  one power too weak.

**Conclusion.**  Part (C) is reduced (§97) to a single true, sharply-bounded statement that is
**not reachable from Mathlib's current special-function API**.  Filling it is a self-contained
development: the Weierstrass product for `Γ` (or `log Γ`'s Euler–Maclaurin expansion), its
`logDeriv`, and the resulting asymptotic.  There is a natural home for the result — a
`Complex.digamma` growth lemma upstream in Mathlib — which is the right place for it, since it is
special-function theory and not specific to this development.

`./check.sh --all` green over **27** files.

## 99. Count bound on an arbitrary interval (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-0b76cf87`, round 71.

**Proved.** [`011/lean/DirichletZeroCount2.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/011/lean/DirichletZeroCount2.lean):

* **`dirichletZeroCountIn_le_of_criticalStrip`** — the general-interval form of §90: for any
  `t₀ < t₁` and any `Z` satisfying §83's hypotheses (including the four-sided `hno`),

  `dirichletZeroCountIn χ t₀ t₁ ≤ C0·(1 + log(q(T+2)))·(1 + |t₁ − t₀|)/π`

  for `|t₀|, |t₁| ≤ T`, `T ≥ 0`.

**Why this is the piece the shift argument needs.**  To handle a `T` for which the rectangle
`[0,1]×[T,T+2]` has a zero on a horizontal side, one moves the rectangle; comparing the count over
the original interval with the count over the moved one requires a bound on an **arbitrary** interval,
not just on `(T, T+1]`.  §90's rectangle happened to be height `2` over `T`; this version decouples
the two.

**The one subtlety.**  `dirichletZeroCountIn` counts zeros with `Im ≤ t₁`, while §83's `Z` lies in the
*open* strip `Im < t₁`.  These agree **because of `hno`**: a zero with `Im = t₁` would lie on the
closed rectangle's boundary but not in `Z`, which `hno` forbids.  So `hZall'` (with `≤ t₁`) follows
from §83's `hZall` (with `< t₁`) plus `hno` — a case split on `z.im < t₁` versus `z.im = t₁`.

**Verification.**  `./check.sh --all` green over **27** files; footprint
`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

**Where this leaves `hbd`.**  Of the four sides:
* `Im = t₀`, `Im = t₁` — now reducible to discreteness of the zeros plus this interval bound;
* `Re = 0`, `Re = 1` — needs `L(1+it, χ) ≠ 0`, i.e. non-vanishing on the line `Re s = 1`, which
  Mathlib does **not** have (only `LSeries_ne_zero_of_one_lt_re`).

## 100. The shift lemma (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-0b76cf87`, round 72.

**Proved.** [`011/lean/DirichletZeroCount2.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/011/lean/DirichletZeroCount2.lean):

* **`exists_delta_avoiding`** — for any finite `S : Finset ℝ` and any `t₀, t₁`, there is `δ ∈ (0,1]`
  with `t₀ - δ ∉ S` and `t₁ - δ ∉ S`.

**Why.**  A finite set cannot cover the interval `(0,1]`: the set of bad `δ` is the union of the two
images of `S` under `s ↦ t₀ - s` and `s ↦ t₁ - s`, which is finite, while `Set.Ioc 0 1` is infinite
(`Set.Ioc_infinite`).  Proved by contradiction: a finite superset of `(0,1]` would make it finite.

**Role.**  This is the crux of `hbd`'s **horizontal** half.  If a zero of `dirichletCompleted χ` lies
on `Im = T` or `Im = T + 2`, one shifts the rectangle down by `δ`: the relevant imaginary parts are
finitely many (the zeros in the compact `[0,1] × [T-1, T+2]`), so §99's arbitrary-interval count bound
can be applied to the shifted rectangle `(T-δ, T+2-δ]`, which still contains `(T, T+1]` when `δ ≤ 1`.

**Verification.**  `./check.sh --all` green over **27** files; footprint
`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

**Remaining for `hbd`.**  Only the assembly of the shift (choosing `δ` from the finite set of
imaginary parts, building `Z` for the shifted rectangle, and comparing the two counts) plus the
**vertical** sides `Re = 0, 1`, which need `L(1+it,χ) ≠ 0` — a Mathlib gap.

## 101. Count comparison for the shift (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-0b76cf87`, round 73.

**Proved.** [`011/lean/DirichletZeroCount2.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/011/lean/DirichletZeroCount2.lean):

* **`dirichletZeroCount_le_countIn_shift`** — for `δ ∈ (0,1]`,
  `dirichletZeroCount χ T ≤ dirichletZeroCountIn χ (T-δ) (T+2-δ)`.

Simply `(T, T+1] ⊆ (T-δ, T+2-δ]`: `δ > 0` gives the lower bound, `δ ≤ 1` the upper.  Proved with
`Set.ncard_le_ncard`, the larger set being finite by compactness
(`IsCompact.inter_dirichletLZeros_finite` on `[0,1] × [T-δ, T+2-δ]`).

**Together §§99–101 now give both ingredients of `hbd`'s horizontal half:**
* §99 — a count bound on the **shifted** interval;
* §100 — existence of a `δ` avoiding the finitely many imaginary parts of zeros;
* §101 — the comparison between the original count and the shifted count.

What remains for that half is purely the packaging: build the finite set of imaginary parts from the
compactness finiteness, apply §100, assemble `Z` for the shifted rectangle with `exists_Z_of_hbd`
(§92) and `logDerivIntegrable_of_hbd` (§93), apply §99, and chain with §101.

(iii) `log_absorb` — each set up on its own, plus a three-line assembly, worked.  This is §90's
lesson (*abstract at the point of friction*) confirmed a **third** time: the friction was the shape

## 107. Library audit: the two remaining gaps confirmed (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-0b76cf87`, round 79.

Having been wrong once about what Mathlib contains (§106), I audited the whole
`Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/` directory (22 files) rather than trusting a narrow grep.

**Findings.**
* **No convexity/growth bound for `L` in the critical strip.**  The `isBigO` hits in
  `AbstractFuncEq.lean` and `Basic.lean` concern `LSeries`/Mellin coefficient decay, not `L(s,χ)`
  growth in `1/2 ≤ Re s ≤ 1`.  So `CriticalStripLogDerivBound`'s critical-strip range has no entry
  point in Mathlib.
* **`RiemannZetaLogDeriv.lean`** (contributed by Terence Tao) proves the logarithmic-derivative
  functional equation for **`ζ`**:  `ζ'/ζ(s) = −ζ'/ζ(1−s) + log(2π) − ψ(s) + (π/2)·tan(πs/2)`.
  This is the right *template* for the `L` version, and it also confirms the pattern that
  digamma enters through the archimedean factor.  But it is stated for `ζ` only, and — more
  importantly — the functional equation by itself does **not** bound `L'/L` on `1/2 ≤ Re s ≤ 1`:
  it maps that strip to itself (`s ↦ 1−s`), so a growth input is still needed.  At `σ = 1/2` it is
  self-referential.
* **No complex Stirling asymptotic** (as §98 established): `Stirling.lean` is factorial-only.

**Conclusion.**  The route is complete modulo exactly two inputs, and both are *genuinely* absent
from Mathlib — now confirmed by a full-directory audit rather than a targeted grep:

| # | input | what it needs |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `CriticalStripLogDerivBound` on `1/2 ≤ σ ≤ 1` | convexity/growth bound for `L(s,χ)` in the strip |
| 2 | `DigammaGrowthBound σ0` | `ψ(z) = log z + O(1/|z|)`, i.e. the digamma/Stirling asymptotic for complex argument |

**README corrected** (§107): its older "state at goal `goal-0b76cf87`" section still listed `hbd` as
a remaining hypothesis; a correction block now records that `hbd` is discharged and that exactly two
inputs remain.

`./check.sh --all` green over **27** files.

is factorial-only and whose `Complex.digamma` has no series or asymptotic.  A route *does* exist —
`GammaSeq_tendsto_Gamma` + `TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn.deriv` would give
`ψ = lim logDeriv (GammaSeq · n)`, hence the series — but it is a substantial development.

**Remaining inputs for a fully hypothesis-free route — exactly two, both audited as absent (§107):**

| input | needs |
|---|---|
| `CriticalStripLogDerivBound` on `1/2 ≤ σ ≤ 1` | convexity/growth bound for `L(s,χ)` in the strip (`PhragmenLindelof.lean` and `completedLFunction_one_sub` exist, so the route is open but multi-round) |
| `DigammaGrowthBound σ0` | the digamma/Stirling asymptotic for complex argument |

**Methodology produced (four instances of one pattern).**  When a *statement* will not elaborate,
wrap the expensive subterm in an `@[irreducible] def` (§80).  When a *proof term* will not, abstract
the composition so its statement forgets the expensive subterms (§90).  When that still fails, cut
the statement in half where the two normalforms meet (§93).  And when a monolithic proof of a
*trivial* packaging step keeps failing, split it into stated lemmas — which succeeded first time
(§104).  Finally: **audit the library directory-by-directory before declaring a gap** (§106: a
three-file development had been searched in two files, and one of three named gaps vanished).

## 109. **Second false hypothesis: `CriticalStripLogDerivBound`** (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-e883bde9` (new), round 1.  Found while beginning part (A) — the same defect class as §96.

**The defect.**  `CriticalStripLogDerivBound χ` is stated as

  `∃ C > 0, ∀ σ ∈ [1/2, 2], ∀ t, ‖Λ_χ'/Λ_χ(σ + it)‖ ≤ C·(1 + log(q(|t|+2)))`

where `Λ_χ'/Λ_χ = logDeriv (dirichletCompleted χ)`.  But `dirichletCompleted χ` **has zeros in the
critical strip** (`0 < Re s < 1` — the nontrivial zeros).  At a zero `ρ`, `logDeriv f s ∼ 1/(s − ρ)`,
so `‖logDeriv‖ → ∞` as `s → ρ`.  **No such `C` exists.**  The hypothesis is unsatisfiable, so
§§83/90/94/95 and §106's `riemannVonMangoldtDensity_of_interface` are **vacuous**.

This is exactly §96's failure mode: a `Prop` introduced to name a gap, never checked for
satisfiability.  §96 fixed `DigammaGrowthBound`; I did **not** then sweep the other interfaces.  That
sweep is part (C) of this goal and should have been done then.

**But the fix is available, and the assembly already provides the needed side condition.**  Reading
§83's proof: `hkey` is applied only at `(x, t₀)`, `(1, y)`, `(x, t₁)` — points on the **boundary** of
the closed rectangle `[0,1] × [t₀,t₁]`, hence **not** in the open rectangle, hence `∉ Z`, hence
nonzero by `hno`.  So the corrected statement

  `∀ σ ∈ [1/2, 2], ∀ t, dirichletCompleted χ (σ + it) ≠ 0 → ‖Λ_χ'/Λ_χ(σ + it)‖ ≤ C·(1 + log(q(|t|+2)))`

is *true* (the standard bound holds away from zeros) and is **satisfied at every point of use**.  The
fix is a chain of signature changes (§83 → §90 → §94 → §95 → `DirichletZeroCount2`), not new
mathematics.

**Action.**  Restate `CriticalStripLogDerivBound` with the zero-free hypothesis and propagate; then
part (A)'s original content — the convexity bound for `L` in the strip — becomes the *mathematical*
task, replacing "prove a false statement".

### 109a. The fix, applied and verified

`CriticalStripLogDerivBound` is now

```lean
def CriticalStripLogDerivBound (χ) : Prop :=
  ∃ C > 0, ∀ σ ∈ [1/2, 2], ∀ t,
    dirichletCompleted χ (σ + it) ≠ 0 →
      ‖Λ_χ'/Λ_χ(σ + it)‖ ≤ C * (1 + log(q(|t|+2)))
```

and the same zero-free hypothesis was threaded through §83, §90, §94, §95 and the explicit-constant
forms in `DirichletZeroCount2.lean` (**5 signatures**, all patched in one pass).

**Only §83 needed proof changes**, exactly as §109 predicted: its three call sites (`hc0`, `hc1`,
`hc2`) are points on the *boundary* of the closed rectangle, so they are `∉ Z` and `hno` supplies
`dirichletCompleted χ u ≠ 0` directly.  The three sub-proofs are one-liners from `hmem`
(`t₀ < u.im`, `u.re < 1`, `u.im < t₁` respectively).

`./check.sh --all` green over **27** files; only axioms `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`;
no `sorry`, `axiom`, `admit`, `native_decide`, `maxHeartbeats`.

**Consequence.**  The hypothesis is now **true** (the standard `|L'/L| ≪ log T` bound holds on
zero-free sets), so §§83/90/94/95 and `riemannVonMangoldtDensity_of_interface` are **no longer
vacuous**.  Part (A) of this goal is thereby *well-posed*: the remaining mathematical task is the
convexity bound for `L` in the strip, on zero-free regions.

**Process note for part (C).**  This defect was found only because the new goal sent me back into
part (A).  §96 fixed one false hypothesis; I did not then sweep the rest.  **The sweep should be
routine after any such fix** — and it is cheap: for each named `Prop` interface, ask "is this
satisfiable?"  The four interfaces in this development are now all checked:
`RootNumberSign` (satisfiable, §45), `CompletedLFunctionConj` (satisfiable),
`CriticalStripLogDerivBound` (**was false**, now fixed), `DigammaGrowthBound` (**was false**, fixed §96).

## 111. Parts (A) and (B) share one root cause (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-e883bde9`, round 3.  **Investigation, recorded as a finding.**

**Part (A) route (convexity bound for `L` in the strip).**  The standard proof is:
1. `L(σ+it) ≪ 1` for `σ > 1` — **available** (Dirichlet series).
2. `L(σ+it) ≪ |t|^{1/2-σ}` for `σ < 0` — via the functional equation
   `L(s) = ε·γ(1−s)·L(1−s)/γ(s)` (`IsPrimitive.completedLFunction_one_sub` gives the `Λ` version), where
   `L(1−s)` is bounded since `Re(1−s) > 1`.  **This step needs a bound on the Gamma ratio**
   `γ(1−s)/γ(s)`, i.e. `‖Γ(x+it)/Γ(x′+it)‖ = O(|t|^{x−x′})`.
3. Phragmén–Lindelöf to interpolate — **available**: `Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/PhragmenLindelof.lean`
   has `horizontal_strip`/`vertical_strip`.

**The obstruction.**  Step 2 is complex Stirling.  I audited every file of
`Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Gamma/` (`Basic`, `Beta`, `BohrMollerup`, `Deligne`, `Deriv`,
`Digamma`) and grepped the whole `Mathlib/Analysis` tree for `‖·‖`-bounds on `Complex.Gamma`: **there
are none.**  `BohrMollerup.lean` is real-only (`logGammaSeq`, `tendsto_log_gamma` at real arguments);
`Stirling.lean` is factorial-only (§98).

**Conclusion — one root cause, two interfaces.**  Both remaining interfaces need the same missing
ingredient:

| interface | needs |
|---|---|
| `CriticalStripLogDerivBound` on `1/2 ≤ σ ≤ 1` | convexity bound for `L`, hence **complex Gamma bounds** |
| `DigammaGrowthBound σ0` | `ψ(z) = log z + O(1/|z|)`, hence **complex Gamma asymptotics** |

So the natural deliverable is a single upstream Mathlib contribution — bounds/asymptotics for
`Complex.Gamma` and `Complex.digamma` on vertical lines — rather than two unrelated ones.  That
reframing is itself the useful output of this round: the goal's parts (A) and (B) are not independent
tasks.

**Caveat, stated honestly.**  I have shown that the *standard* routes need Gamma asymptotics, and
that Mathlib has none.  I have **not** proved that no elementary workaround exists (e.g. via the
reflection and duplication formulas, which do relate `Γ` values at different arguments).  A
workaround would still have to deliver a uniform `O(|t|^{x-x'})` ratio bound, which is Stirling's
content; I would not expect a cheap one.

## 112. First Γ bound: `norm_Gamma_le_Gamma_re` (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-e883bde9`, rounds 4–7.

**Proved.**  New module [`011/lean/GammaBounds.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/011/lean/GammaBounds.lean):

* **`norm_Gamma_le_Gamma_re`** — for `Re s > 0`, `‖Complex.Gamma s‖ ≤ Real.Gamma s.re`.

From Euler's integral (`Complex.Gamma_eq_integral` + `GammaIntegral`): the triangle inequality turns
`‖∫ x^{s-1}e^{-x}‖` into `∫ |x^{s-1}|e^{-x} = ∫ x^{Re s - 1}e^{-x} = Γ(Re s)`
(`Complex.norm_cpow_eq_rpow_re_of_pos`, then `Complex.GammaIntegral_ofReal`).

Added to `check.sh --all` (now **28** files) and `AxiomsL.lean`.  Footprint
`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

**Honest note on cost.**  This one elementary lemma took four rounds, almost entirely on API friction
(`GammaIntegral`'s integrand normal form, `ofReal` coercions, the real/complex integral conversion).
It is a genuine first brick — the development had **no** Γ bound before — but it is *not* sufficient
for either remaining interface: §111 established that those need a **ratio** bound
`‖Γ(x+it)/Γ(x′+it)‖ = O(|t|^{x−x′})`, i.e. a lower bound on `‖Γ‖` as well as an upper one, which is
Stirling's content.

**Assessment of scale.**  The path to the goal's success condition is: complex Stirling for `Γ`
(upper **and** lower bounds on vertical lines), then `ψ` asymptotics, then the convexity bound for
`L` via `PhragmenLindelof.horizontal_strip`, then `L′/L` on zero-free sets.  Each stage is a
substantial development and Mathlib supplies none of them.  I will continue on the bricks, but the
goal as stated is unlikely to close within the remaining rounds.

## 114. The `Λ′/Λ` functional equation is sign-only (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-e883bde9`, round 9.

Checking what the development already has, I found
**`logDeriv_dirichletCompleted_one_sub`** (`DirichletCompletedSymmetry.lean`):

  `Λ_χ′/Λ_χ(1 − s) = − Λ_χ′/Λ_χ(s)`

— **no Gamma factor and no `ψ` term**, because `dirichletCompleted` is *normalised*
(`Λ(1−s) = ε·Λ(s)` with `ε = rootNumber χ = ±1`, the sign cancelling in the log-derivative).  This
is a genuine simplification over the `ζ` situation, where Tao's `logDeriv_riemannZeta_one_sub`
carries `log(2π)`, `ψ s` and `(π/2)tan(πs/2)`.

Combined with `logDeriv_dirichletCompleted_conj` (conjugation symmetry), we get
`‖Λ′/Λ(σ+it)‖ = ‖Λ′/Λ(1−σ+it)‖`: the strip bound is **symmetric** under `σ ↦ 1−σ`.

**Consequence for part (A).**  Two things follow, one helping and one not.
* *Helping*: the reflection step contributes **no digamma** — so part (A)'s strip bound does not
  itself require part (B).  The coupling asserted in §111 is therefore only through the *convexity*
  bound, not through the functional equation for `Λ′/Λ`.
* *Not helping*: `σ ↦ 1−σ` maps `[1/2, 1]` to `[0, 1/2]` — the strip is invariant, so this relation
  alone cannot reach the half-plane `σ > 1` where the bound is already proved.  The interpolation
  input (convexity for `L`, hence complex Stirling) is still required.

So the honest count for part (A) is: **lemmas 1 and 2 of §113 (the Gamma bounds and ratio) and
lemma 4 (convexity), but not lemma 3 (`ψ`)**.  That is a genuine narrowing of the gap.

## 115. Part (B)'s reduction had a hole — in exactly the range used (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-e883bde9`, round 10.  **A real gap in the reduction, found and fixed.**

**The hole.**  §97's `digammaGrowthBound_of_stripBound` takes the shift `n : ℕ` with
`σ0 - n ∈ [1,2]`, so it covers `σ0 ≥ 1` **only**.  But §80 needs `DigammaGrowthBound (c/2)` with
`c > 1`, i.e. `σ0 = c/2 > 1/2` — and for `c ∈ (1,2)`, `σ0 ∈ (1/2, 1)`.  So the reduction did **not
cover the case it is used in.**  Had part (B) ever been "closed" via §97 alone, §80 would still have
had an uncovered hypothesis.

**Proved.**  [`011/lean/DirichletMellinPrereq.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/011/lean/DirichletMellinPrereq.lean):

* **`digammaGrowthBound_of_stripBound_small`** — for `0 < σ0 ≤ 1`, the strip bound on `[1,2]` gives
  `DigammaGrowthBound σ0`.  Run the recursion *up* by one, `ψ(s) = ψ(s+1) − s⁻¹` (Mathlib's
  `Complex.digamma_apply_add_nat` at `n = 1`), which costs only `1/σ0`, bounded by `σ0 ≤ ‖s‖`.

Note `1/σ0` is finite precisely because `σ0 > 0` — for `σ0 → 0+` it blows up, matching the pole of
`ψ` at `0`.

Footprint `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`; `./check.sh --all` green over **28** files.

**This is the pattern worth noting.**  §96 corrected the *statement* of `DigammaGrowthBound`, §97
reduced it — but the reduction was never checked against its *use site*.  A hypothesis can be true,
and its reduction sound, and still not cover the range the consumer needs.  This is the third variant
of the same lesson in this goal (§96 false statement, §109 false statement, §115 insufficient
coverage), and it is cheap to guard against: **check each reduction against the range its consumer
actually instantiates.**

**The hole.**  Grepping who *calls* §97 showed: **nobody**.  `digammaGrowthBound_of_stripBound` takes

## 117. **§109's fix was insufficient: the pointwise form is still false** (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-e883bde9`, round 12.  This is the most consequential finding of the goal.

**The defect.**  §109 corrected `CriticalStripLogDerivBound` by adding the pointwise zero-free
hypothesis:

  `∃ C > 0, ∀ σ ∈ [1/2, 2], ∀ t, Λ_χ(σ+it) ≠ 0 → ‖Λ_χ′/Λ_χ(σ+it)‖ ≤ C·(1 + log(q(|t|+2)))`

**It is still false.**  `logDeriv f x = deriv f x / f x` is `rfl`-definitionally `deriv f x / f x`, so
near a *simple* zero `ρ`, `Λ(x) ≈ Λ′(ρ)(x − ρ)` and hence `Λ′/Λ(x) ≈ 1/(x − ρ) → ∞`.  Taking
`x = ρ + ε` with `ε` arbitrarily small gives a point that **satisfies the hypothesis** (`Λ(x) ≠ 0`
since zeros are isolated) while the left side blows up — and the right side
`C·(1 + log(q(|Im ρ| + 2)))` is a **fixed constant**, since `|t|` is pinned to `|Im ρ|`.  So the
implication fails.

**Why §109 missed it.**  §109 asked "is the hypothesis satisfiable?" — and `Λ(σ+it) ≠ 0` *is*
satisfiable.  The right question is stronger: **does the hypothesis control the quantity being
bounded?**  Non-vanishing at a point does not control `deriv f / f` at that point; only *distance to
the zeros* does.

**Scope of the damage.**  §109 asserted "the assembly already provides the needed side condition".
That is wrong.  §83's `hkey` is applied on the three boundary segments, which are compact and
zero-free — so `‖Λ′/Λ‖` is *finite* there, but its bound depends on the segments' **distance to the
zeros**, which can be arbitrarily small.  A zero at `τ_ρ` just above `t₀` makes `‖Λ′/Λ‖` on the
segment `Im = t₀` as large as `1/(τ_ρ − t₀)`.

**What is actually true (the standard input).**  Two facts hold, and neither is pointwise:
1. **Contour bound**: `∫_{∂R} ‖Λ′/Λ‖ = O(log T)`, because the singularities near the boundary
   contribute only **logarithmically** (`∫ ‖1/(x−ρ)‖ ≈ log(1/δ)`, not `1/δ`).  §81's route is
   pointwise (`M · length`) and therefore *lossy*, though not itself false.
2. **Spacing**: zeros in `[0,T]` number `~ (T/2π)log T`, so consecutive gaps are `~ 2π/log T`; hence
   `dist(s, zeros) ≫ 1/log T` for the boundary, giving `‖Λ′/Λ‖ = O(log T)` pointwise — but *only*
   using the spacing/zero-count theorem.

**So the honest input is a bound on the contour, or a distance-conditioned bound plus a spacing
theorem — not pointwise non-vanishing.**

**Recorded as a correction to §109.**  The `CriticalStripLogDerivBound` statement needs the
distance condition (or a contour form); §109's version must not be used as-is.  This is the fourth
variant of one lesson (§§96, 109, 115, 117), and the sharpest form of it is:

> A hypothesis must control the quantity being bounded, not merely be satisfiable.

---

## 118. Design conclusion: the input must be a *contour* bound (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-e883bde9`, round 13.  Follows from §117.

**Two possible fixes, with the tradeoff.**

*Fix 1 — distance-conditioned pointwise.*  Add to `CriticalStripLogDerivBound` a hypothesis that
`dist(s, zeros) ≥ 1/(1+log(q(|t|+2)))`.  The statement becomes **true** (the standard bound).  But
§83 then needs that distance condition at its three boundary segments, and supplying it requires the
**zero-spacing theorem** — zeros in `[0,T]` are `~ (T/2π)log T` in number, so gaps are `~2π/log T`.
That theorem is *downstream* of the count bound in this development (`RiemannVonMangoldtDensity` was
derived **from** the log-derivative input), so this route is **circular** as things stand.

*Fix 2 — contour (integral) bound.*  Replace the pointwise input by a bound on the **integral** of
`‖Λ′/Λ‖` along the boundary.  This is the route that is actually correct, and it is correct
**without** spacing:

  `∑_Z m = Im(rightPath)/π`,  so  `∑_Z m ≤ ‖rightPath‖/π ≤ (∫_{∂R} ‖Λ′/Λ‖)/π`,

and `∫_{∂R} ‖Λ′/Λ‖ = O(log(qT)·(1+|t₁−t₀|))` by the standard contour estimate — the singularities
near the boundary contribute only **logarithmically** (§117 point 1), so no spacing input is needed.
§81 (`dirichletCompleted_zeroCount_le_of_contour`) already takes a bound `M` on `‖rightPath‖`, so
Fix 2 plugs in **without touching §81** — only the interface and the derivation of `‖rightPath‖ ≤ B`
from the contour integral change.

**Conclusion: Fix 2 is the right one.**  It is additive (a new interface + a short lemma from
`‖∫‖ ≤ ∫‖·‖`), avoids the circularity, and makes §83 non-vacuous with a hypothesis that is *true*.

**Not yet executed.**  The restructure is mechanical but touches ~7 declarations, and it does not on
its own make `CriticalStripLogDerivBound` a *theorem* — the contour estimate still needs the
convexity bound for `L` (§113 lemmas 1, 2, 4).  So the goal's success condition remains out of reach
in this session; Fix 2 is the correct starting point for a successor.

**Added to the README process guidance** as a sixth rule: *a hypothesis must control the quantity
being bounded, not merely be satisfiable* — with §96, §109, §115 and §117 as the four instances.

---

## 119. **Fix 2 executed: the contour interface replaces the false pointwise one** (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-e883bde9`, round 14.

**What changed.**  `CriticalStripLogDerivBound` is now a **contour (integral)** bound:

```lean
def CriticalStripLogDerivBound (χ) : Prop :=
  ∃ C > 0, ∀ t₀ t₁ T, t₀ < t₁ → |t₀| ≤ T → |t₁| ≤ T → 0 ≤ T →
    (∫ x in 1/2..1, ‖Λ′/Λ(x + t₀i)‖) + (∫ y in t₀..t₁, ‖Λ′/Λ(1 + yi)‖)
      + (∫ x in 1/2..1, ‖Λ′/Λ(x + t₁i)‖)
    ≤ C * (1 + log(q(T+2))) * (1 + |t₁ − t₀|)
```

It bounds the **integral** along the three segments of `rightPath`, exactly the quantity the
argument-principle count consumes.

**Why this is the right statement (§§117–118).**  The old pointwise form
`Λ(σ+it) ≠ 0 → ‖Λ′/Λ(σ+it)‖ ≤ C·(1+log(q(|t|+2)))` was **false**: `Λ′/Λ` is unbounded *near* a
zero while being defined there.  The integral bound is the correct statement — the singularities
contribute only logarithmically — and, unlike a distance-conditioned pointwise form, it needs **no
zero-spacing input**, so it avoids the circularity identified in §118.

**Propagation.**  5 signatures in `DirichletZeroCount2.lean` plus the definition and §83.
**Only §83 needed proof changes — and it got simpler**: the pointwise `hkey`, the three segment
bounds `hc0/hc1/hc2`, and the whole `log`-absorption step (including its `Real.exp` estimate) are all
**gone**, replaced by `‖∫‖ ≤ ∫‖·‖` on each segment followed by the contour hypothesis.  §90, §94,
§95, §106 pass `hcs` through unchanged.

`./check.sh --all` green over **28** files; only axioms `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`;

## 122. **Correction to §121**: `CompletedLFunctionConj` is a genuine gap (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-e883bde9`, round 17.  **My §121 optimism was wrong; recorded.**

**What I claimed in §121.**  That `CompletedLFunctionConj` was "likely the third gap that isn't a
gap", on the strength of `Complex.Gamma_conj` existing — i.e. that only the `L`-half
`LFunction χ (conj s) = conj (LFunction χ s)` remained.

**Why that is wrong.**  `completedLFunction χ` unfolds to

```lean
ZMod.completedLFunction Φ s = N^(-s) * ∑ j, Φ j * completedHurwitzZetaEven (toAddCircle j) s
                            + N^(-s) * ∑ j, Φ j * completedHurwitzZetaOdd  (toAddCircle j) s
```

(`ZMod.lean:295`).  So the conjugation property needs **Hurwitz-zeta** conjugation — and there is no
`completedHurwitzZetaEven_conj`.  Worse, the argument is `a : UnitAddCircle`, a **circle**: `conj`
is not even defined on it, so the property has to be stated and proved at the level of the *modulus*
parameter, not the circle element.

So `CompletedLFunctionConj` requires a genuine (if narrow) development: conjugation symmetry of
`completedHurwitzZetaEven/Odd`, then of `ZMod.completedLFunction`, then of `completedLFunction`.

**Is it *used*?**  Yes — `dirichletCompleted_routeBCount` passes it to
`logDeriv_dirichletCompleted_reflection`, Route B's reflection hypothesis.  So it is not vestigial.

**Also corrected: the `L`-half's cost.**  Even setting Hurwitz aside, `LFunction_conj` for real `χ`
needs conjugation of `LSeries` at `Re s > 1` plus an identity-theorem extension; Mathlib has
`LFunction_eq_LSeries` and `differentiableAt_LFunction`, but no `LSeries_conj`.

**Lesson (a seventh rule, and it cuts the other way).**  I have been finding "gaps that aren't gaps"
(§106, §120) — but this shows the *opposite* error is equally available: **assuming a gap is shallow
because a related lemma exists.**  `Complex.Gamma_conj` existing says nothing about the Hurwitz-zeta
layer underneath.  A gap is only shallow if its **entire dependency chain** is shallow — so check the
*unfolding* of the definition, not the existence of a similarly-named lemma.

## 123. **Part (B) is elementary** — the bound computation (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-e883bde9`, round 18.  I worked out the mathematics; it is much cheaper than §113 assumed.

**The limit formula.**  `GammaSeq s n = n^s·n!/∏_{j<n+1}(s+j)` gives, by the product rule,

  `logDeriv (GammaSeq · n) s = log n − ∑_{j<n+1} 1/(s+j)  =:  L_n(s)`,

and `L_n(s) → ψ(s) = logDeriv Γ s` because `GammaSeq · n → Γ` (Mathlib's `GammaSeq_tendsto_Gamma`),
`deriv (GammaSeq · n) → deriv Γ` (dominated convergence on
`GammaSeq_eq_approx_Gamma_integral`: `Γ_n(s) = ∫_0^n (1−x/n)^n x^{s−1}dx`, dominated by
`e^{−x}x^{σ−1}`), and `Γ(s) ≠ 0` for `Re s > 0`.

**The bound — a two-line estimate, no Stirling.**  Write `s = σ₀ + it`, `σ₀ > 0`.  Split

  `|L_n(s)| ≤ |log n − ∑_{j<n} 1/(σ₀+j)| + |∑_{j<n} (1/(σ₀+j) − 1/(s+j))|`.

*First term `= O(1)`*: `∑_{j<n} 1/(σ₀+j) = log(σ₀+n) − log σ₀ + O(1/n)`, so the difference is
`log n − log(σ₀+n) + log σ₀ + O(1/n) = O(1)`, using `log n − log(σ₀+n) ≤ 0`.

*Second term `= O(log(|t|+2))`*: the difference is `it·∑ 1/((σ₀+j)(s+j))`, so

  `|t|·∑_{j<n} 1/((σ₀+j)·√((σ₀+j)²+t²))`,

split at `σ₀+j ≤ |t|`:
* `σ₀+j ≤ |t|`: `√(…) ≥ |t|`, and `∑_{σ₀+j≤|t|} 1/(σ₀+j) ≤ log(|t|+2)`, giving `≤ log(|t|+2)`;
* `σ₀+j > |t|`: `√(…) ≥ σ₀+j`, giving `|t|·∑ 1/(σ₀+j)² ≤ |t|·(2/|t|) = O(1)`.

Hence `‖L_n(s)‖ ≤ C(1 + log(|t|+2))` **uniformly in `n`**, and since `‖ψ(s)‖ = lim ‖L_n(s)‖`,
`DigammaGrowthBound σ₀` follows for **every** `σ₀ > 0` — directly, bypassing §97/§116.

**Significance.**  §113 listed `norm_digamma_le` as "lemma 3", needing the digamma series.  In fact
**no asymptotic and no Stirling is needed** — only `GammaSeq`'s log-derivative (a product rule) and
this elementary split.  The §113 specification **overstated the gap for part (B)**.

**Remaining formalisation work** (in order, each small):
1. `logDeriv (GammaSeq · n) s = log n − ∑_{j<n+1} 1/(s+j)` (product rule; `logDeriv_prod` exists);
2. `Tendsto (fun n => logDeriv (GammaSeq · n) s) atTop (𝓝 (ψ s))` (dominated convergence);
3. the split estimate above;
4. assemble into `DigammaGrowthBound σ₀`.

## 124. Formalising §123: attempted, reverted, with a concrete recommendation (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-e883bde9`, round 19.

**Attempted.**  `logDeriv_GammaSeq`, the first of §123's four steps:
`logDeriv (GammaSeq · n) s = log n − ∑_{j<n+1} 1/(s+j)`.  Several formulations tried (division form,
product-with-inverse form, `f/g` with explicit types).  Every attempt reached 2–4 residual goals,
mostly on coercion and `Pi`-instance friction rather than mathematics.  **Reverted**;
`./check.sh --all` green over **28** files.

**The specific obstacles, recorded so they are not rediscovered:**
1. `(f / g)` for `f g : ℂ → ℂ` gives `HMul (ℕ → ℂ) (ℂ → ℂ) (ℂ → ℂ)` unless **every** lambda is
   annotated `fun w : ℂ =>` — the binder type is otherwise inferred from the first occurrence.
2. `n !` does not parse inside `(n ! : ℂ)`; use `(Nat.factorial n : ℂ)`.
3. `(fun _ => 1) / g = fun w => (g w)⁻¹` is **not** `rfl` — `one_div` must be used.
4. `fun_prop` cannot discharge `DifferentiableAt ℂ (fun w => (n:ℂ)^w * (Nat.factorial n : ℂ)) s`
   without help: `const_cpow` differentiability needs `n ≠ 0` supplied as an instance.

**Recommended next attempt (§90's rule).**  Do **not** prove a combined `logDeriv` identity.  Instead
state the *bound* directly and abstract the friction away:
* `L_n(s) := Complex.log n − ∑_{j<n+1} (s + j)⁻¹` as a **definition** (`@[irreducible]`);
* prove `logDeriv (GammaSeq · n) s = L_n s` in a lemma whose **statement** mentions only `L_n`;
* prove the §123 split estimate about `L_n` **separately**, with no `GammaSeq`/`logDeriv` in sight.
That is exactly the §90 pattern — abstract the composition so each half's statement forgets the
other's normalform — and it was what unblocked §90, §93 and §104 after monoliths failed.

**Status.**  §123's mathematics stands (verified by hand, no Stirling needed).  The formalisation is
~4 lemmas of `Gamma`/`cpow` API work; the recommended decomposition should make each tractable.

## 125. **Correction to §123's split** — the `log` growth is in `Re`, not `Im` (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-e883bde9`, round 20.

Re-deriving §123's estimate carefully, I find I attributed the growth to the wrong component.
Writing `s = σ₀ + it` and `L_n(s) = log n − ∑_{j<n+1} 1/(s+j)`:

  `Re L_n = log n − ∑_{j<n+1} (σ₀+j)/((σ₀+j)²+t²)`,
  `Im L_n = t·∑_{j<n+1} 1/((σ₀+j)²+t²)`.

**`Im L_n` is `O(1)`** — this is the *opposite* of what §123 said.  Since
`∑_{j≥0} 1/((σ₀+j)²+t²) ≤ 1/(σ₀²+t²) + ∫_0^∞ dx/((σ₀+x)²+t²) ≤ 1/t² + π/(2|t|)`, multiplying by `|t|`
gives `|Im L_n| ≤ 1/|t| + π/2`.

**`Re L_n` carries the `log`**, and needs *two-sided* control:
* **Upper bound on `Re L_n`** (i.e. lower bound on `∑`): split at `σ₀+j ≤ |t|`.  For `σ₀+j ≤ |t|`,
  `(σ₀+j)²+t² ≤ 2t²` so the term is `≥ (σ₀+j)/(2t²)`, summing to `≳ 1/4`; for `σ₀+j > |t|`,
  `(σ₀+j)²+t² ≤ 2(σ₀+j)²` so the term is `≥ 1/(2(σ₀+j))`, summing to `≈ ½(log n − log|t|)`.
  Hence `Re L_n ≤ ½log|t| + O(1)`.
* **Lower bound on `Re L_n`**: `∑_{j<n+1}(σ₀+j)/((σ₀+j)²+t²) ≤ ∑_{j<n+1} 1/(σ₀+j) ≈ log n`, so
  `Re L_n ≥ −O(1)`.

So `|Re L_n| ≤ ½log|t| + O(1)` and `|Im L_n| = O(1)`, giving `‖L_n(s)‖ ≤ C(1 + log(|t|+2))`
**uniformly in `n`** — §123's conclusion stands, its attribution corrected.

**Why this matters for formalisation.**  The estimate is now *finite-sum real analysis*: monotone
comparisons of `∑ 1/(σ₀+j)` against `log`, and the split at `σ₀+j = |t|`.  **No `GammaSeq`, no
`logDeriv`, no `cpow`** — so it is a good candidate for §124's step 3, done *first* and in isolation
from the `Gamma` API friction.

## 127. Two finds that make §125's estimate tractable (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-e883bde9`, round 22.

**Find 1 — `Mathlib/NumberTheory/Harmonic/` exists.**  Directory-by-directory audit (the §106 rule)
turned up `NumberTheory/Harmonic/Bounds.lean` with

* `log_add_one_le_harmonic (n) : Real.log (n+1) ≤ harmonic n`
* `harmonic_le_one_add_log (n) : harmonic n ≤ 1 + Real.log n`
* `log_le_harmonic_floor`, `harmonic_floor_le_one_add_log` (real arguments)

plus `GammaDeriv.lean` (`deriv_Gamma_nat`, `eulerMascheroniConstant_eq_neg_deriv`) and
`EulerMascheroni.lean`.  These give §125's **first bracket** bound directly:
`∑_{j<n+1} 1/(σ₀+j) ≤ 1/σ₀ + harmonic n ≤ 1/σ₀ + 1 + log n`.

**Find 2 — the tail sum telescopes, so no integral comparison is needed.**  §125's second bracket is
`|t|·∑_{j<n+1} 1/((σ₀+j)·√((σ₀+j)²+t²))`, split at `σ₀+j ≤ |t|`:

* **head** (`σ₀+j ≤ |t|`): `√(…) ≥ |t|`, so the whole term contributes
  `∑_{σ₀+j≤|t|} 1/(σ₀+j) ≤ 1/σ₀ + 1 + log(|t|+2)` — **Find 1**;
* **tail** (`σ₀+j > |t|`): `√(…) ≥ σ₀+j`, so the whole term is
  `|t|·∑_{σ₀+j>|t|} 1/(σ₀+j)² ≤ |t|·1/(σ₀+|t|) ≤ 1`,

  using `1/(σ₀+j)² ≤ 1/((σ₀+j−1)(σ₀+j)) = 1/(σ₀+j−1) − 1/(σ₀+j)` and **telescoping** —
  no `Finset.sum_le_integral`, no order theory, just `Finset.sum_range_sub` or induction.

**So both brackets are boundable from Mathlib's harmonic bounds plus a telescoping sum.**  §113's
"needs complex Stirling" entry for `norm_digamma_le` was doubly wrong: no Stirling (§123) and no deep
real analysis either.  This is the third time in this goal that a **directory audit replaced a
perceived hard ingredient with an existing lemma** (§§106, 127), and the second that an *integral
comparison* turned out to be avoidable by telescoping.

## 128. **The sum–integral comparison API exists** (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-e883bde9`, round 23.  Fourth "perceived-difficulty-is-an-unaudited-library" find.

Reading `Mathlib/NumberTheory/Harmonic/Bounds.lean` (found in §127) to see how *it* proves its own
bounds, I saw it import and use

  **`Mathlib/Analysis/SumIntegralComparisons.lean`**

which contains the complete monotone sum–integral comparison API I had been assuming did not exist
and working around by hand:

| lemma | content |
|---|---|
| `AntitoneOn.sum_le_integral` | `∑ f i ≤ ∫ f` |
| `AntitoneOn.integral_le_sum` | `∫ f ≤ ∑ f i` |
| `AntitoneOn.sum_range_le_integral` | the `range` form |
| `AntitoneOn.sum_le_integral_Ico`, `…_Ioc`, `…_of_integrableOn` | interval variants |
| `MonotoneOn.*` | the dual family |
| `sum_Ico_le_integral_of_le`, `integral_le_sum_Ico_of_le` | direct forms |
| `AntitoneOn.summable_of_integrableOn_Ioi(_zero)` | summability corollaries |

**Consequences.**
1. §125's bounds are now routine: `x ↦ 1/(a+x)²` is antitone, so
   `∑_{j<N} 1/(a+j)² ≤ ∫_0^N dx/(a+x)² = 1/a − 1/(a+N) ≤ 1/a` — **cleaner than the telescoping
   argument of §127** (which needed the extra `1/a²` term for the `j = 0` summand).
   The head sum `∑ 1/(a+j) ≤ 1 + log(N+a)` similarly.
2. My §124/§126 recommendation ("do it in ℝ only, avoid `Complex`") is still right, but the reason I
   gave for expecting friction — "no integral comparison in Mathlib" — was **wrong**: the friction
   was purely coercion plumbing, and the real-analysis tooling was there all along.

**Pattern, now with four instances.**  §§106, 120/127, 128: *every* hard ingredient this goal has
needed outside the `Gamma` asymptotics turned out to exist in Mathlib, and was found by **reading an
adjacent file rather than grepping for the name I expected**.  The grep-for-the-expected-name failure
mode is the single most expensive recurring error in this development.

3. `∫ 1/x^2` needs rewriting to `x ^ (-2 : ℤ)` **before** `integral_zpow` applies, via
   `rw [one_div, ← zpow_natCast (n := 2), ← zpow_neg]`.
4. `Finset.sum_range_succ'` produces `1/(b + ↑0)^2`; matching it needs `Nat.cast_zero` in the final
   `simpa`, not just `zero_add`/`add_zero`.
5. `linarith` treats `∑ …` as an atom, so a goal summand written `b + (↑x + 1)` will **not** unify
   with a hypothesis summand written `b + ↑(x + 1)` — the binder form must match exactly.

**Remaining for part (B)**: (3) the `ℂ` split identity (§125), (4) `ψ = lim L_n` and the assembly.
The `ℝ` estimate `|t|·(head + tail) ≤ C(1+log(|t|+2))` now follows from the two lemmas above with
`b = σ₀`, splitting the `σ₀ + j ≤ |t|` case at `N = ⌈|t|⌉`.

## 131. The subtlety that defeated rounds 19–23, stated exactly (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-e883bde9`, round 26.

Recording the precise remaining target for `DigammaGrowthBound` (README §5) forced me to name the
thing that rounds 19–23 kept getting wrong.

**The target** (`σ₀ ≥ 1`, and the bound must be *uniform in `n`*):

  `|t| · ∑_{j<n+1} 1/((σ₀+j)·√((σ₀+j)²+t²))  ≤  5·(1 + log(|t|+2))`.

Two bounds are already proved (§§129–130) and suffice:

* `sum_range_inv_le_log` — used on the **head** `σ₀+j ≤ |t|`;
* `sum_range_inv_sq_le` — used on the **tail**, **reindexed** at `b := σ₀+M`, giving `≤ 2/(σ₀+M) ≤ 2/|t|`.

**The subtlety.**  `sum_range_inv_le_log` bounds by `1 + log N` where `N` is the range length — but
the range length here is `n+1`, and `n` is *the limit variable*.  Applying it directly yields
`O(log n)`, which is **not uniform in `n` and therefore useless**.  The head must be truncated at
`⌈|t|⌉` (splitting once more at `A = |t|`) so that the `log` becomes `log(|t|+2)`.

**This is the real reason rounds 19–23 failed**, and it is not coercion friction as I recorded in
§§124/126/129.  Those rounds attacked `logDeriv_GammaSeq` — the *identity*
`logDeriv (GammaSeq · n) s = log n − ∑ 1/(s+j)` — whose right-hand side genuinely contains `log n`
and therefore genuinely is not uniformly bounded.  **The bound lives not in `L_n` but in the
cancellation between `log n` and `∑_{j<n+1} 1/(σ₀+j)`** — which is precisely what the head/tail split
at `|t|` exploits, and why the *inequality* must be proved before the *identity* rather than derived
from it.

**Corrected lesson.**  §129's "state `ℝ`-valued facts in `ℝ`" was right for the wrong reason: the
obstruction was not the `ℂ` coercions but that **the identity is not uniformly bounded while the
difference is**.  A successor should prove `Lseq_bound` first — proving the identity first is not
merely slower, it is a dead end.

`b > 0`:

* **`abs_div_mul_sqrt_le_abs_div_sq`** — `|t|/(b·√(b²+t²)) ≤ |t|/b²` (tail: `√(b²+t²) ≥ b`).

Both footprints `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`; `./check.sh --all` green over **28** files.

**Progress on `Lseq_bound`.**  With §§129–130 and the two lemmas above, every *ingredient* is now

  `∑_{j<n+1} min(1/(σ₀+j), |t|/(σ₀+j)²) ≤ ∑_{j<M} 1/(σ₀+j) + |t|·∑_{j≥M} 1/(σ₀+j)²`

with `M := ⌈|t|⌉₊` (so `σ₀+M > |t|`), the second sum reindexed to `b := σ₀+M` and bounded by

constant `5`.

## 133. `Lseq_head_bound` proved (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-e883bde9`, round 28.  The head half of `Lseq_bound`.

**Proved** [`011/lean/GammaBounds.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/011/lean/GammaBounds.lean):

* **`Lseq_head_bound`** — for `σ₀ ≥ 1` and `M` a **ceiling** of `|t|` (`|t| ≤ M` and `M < |t|+1`),

  `|t| · ∑_{j<M} 1/((σ₀+j)·√((σ₀+j)²+t²)) ≤ 1 + log(|t|+2)`.

Proof: termwise `abs_div_mul_sqrt_le_inv` (§132) gives `≤ 1/(σ₀+j)`, then `sum_range_inv_le_log`
(§129) gives `≤ 1 + log M ≤ 1 + log(|t|+2)`.  Footprint `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`;
`./check.sh --all` green over **28** files.

**One hypothesis I had omitted, worth recording.**  I first stated the lemma with only
`hM : |t| ≤ M`.  That is **not enough**: `M` must be a *ceiling* of `|t|`, so `M < |t| + 1` is needed
as well — `|t| ≤ M` alone only says `M ≥ |t|` and leaves `M` unbounded above, so `log M ≤ log(|t|+2)`
fails.  This is the same shape as §131: **the bound must be uniform in the parameter, and here `M`
is that parameter.**  A `⌈·⌉`-style bound needs *both* inequalities, not one.

**Remaining for `Lseq_bound`**: the tail lemma
`|t| · ∑_{i<m} 1/((σ₀+M+i)·√((σ₀+M+i)²+t²)) ≤ 2` for `σ₀+M > |t|` — from
`abs_div_mul_sqrt_le_abs_div_sq` (§132) + `sum_range_inv_sq_le` with `b := σ₀+M` (§130), giving
`≤ |t|·2/(σ₀+M) ≤ 2` — then the `Finset.sum_range_add` assembly with `min (n+1) M`, where the case
`n+1 ≤ M` needs the tail to be *empty* rather than merely bounded (§131).

## 138. The real bracket needs `log n`, not `log(n+1)` — a bound in the wrong direction (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-e883bde9`, round 33.  **Attempted `Lseq_real_bracket_abs_le`, reverted after finding a
genuine sign error in my own plan.**

**The claim I tried to prove:** `|log n − ∑_{j<n+1} 1/(σ₀+j)| ≤ log σ₀ + 1` for `σ₀ ≥ 1`, `n ≥ 1`.

**The upper bound is fine.**  `∑ ≥ log(n+1) − log σ₀` (§136), so
`log n − ∑ ≤ log n − log(n+1) + log σ₀ ≤ log σ₀` using `log n ≤ log(n+1)`.  ✓

**The lower bound is where I went wrong.**  I used `sum_range_inv_le_log` (§129), i.e.
`∑ ≤ 1 + log(n+1)`, and concluded `log n − ∑ ≥ −1`.  That is **invalid**: `log(n+1) > log n`, so
`∑ ≤ 1 + log(n+1)` is *weaker* than `∑ ≤ 1 + log n`, and gives
`log n − ∑ ≥ log n − 1 − log(n+1)`, which is **not** bounded below by `−1` — the `log n − log(n+1)`
term is negative and unbounded in the wrong direction.  I had silently assumed `log n ≥ log(n+1)`.

**What is actually true**, and needs one more lemma:
`S = 1/σ₀ + ∑_{j=1}^{n} 1/(σ₀+j) ≤ 1/σ₀ + ∑_{j=1}^{n} 1/j = 1/σ₀ + harmonic n ≤ 2 + log n`,
so `log n − S ≥ −2`, and `|log n − S| ≤ max(log σ₀, 2)`.  The key is to split off the `j = 0` term and
use `harmonic n` (whose bound is `1 + log n`) rather than `harmonic (n+1)` (whose bound is
`1 + log(n+1)`) — **the `+1` inside the logarithm is exactly what breaks it.**

**Recorded as a proof-plan defect, not a library gap.**  Every ingredient existed; the error was in my
own inequality direction, and it is the same species as §§131/133: *an inequality whose shift direction
is not checked*.  A successor should state the harmonic bound with the **same** index as the logarithm.

Build green over **28** files; nothing committed this round.

---

## 139. Sharpened harmonic bound — §138's fix, implemented (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-e883bde9`, round 34.

**Proved** [`011/lean/GammaBounds.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/011/lean/GammaBounds.lean):

* **`sum_range_inv_succ_le_log`** — for `b ≥ 1` and **every** `n`,
  `∑_{j<n+1} 1/(b+j) ≤ 2 + Real.log n`.

Proof: `Finset.sum_range_succ'` splits off the `j = 0` term (bounded by `1` because `b ≥ 1`), leaving
`∑_{j<n} 1/(b+(j+1)) ≤ harmonic n ≤ 1 + log n` by termwise comparison and
`harmonic_le_one_add_log`.  Footprint `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`; `./check.sh --all`
green over **28** files.

**This is exactly §138's diagnosis, cashed in.**  The distinction is entirely in the index:

| lemma | bound | adequate for? |
|---|---|---|
| `sum_range_inv_le_log` (§129) | `∑_{j<N} 1/(b+j) ≤ 1 + log N` | the **upper** bound on `log n − S` ✓ |
| `sum_range_inv_succ_le_log` (§139) | `∑_{j<n+1} 1/(b+j) ≤ 2 + log n` | the **lower** bound ✓ |

With `N = n+1` the first gives `1 + log(n+1)`, whose `log(n+1) > log n` makes it useless for bounding
`log n − S` from below; the second is stated with the logarithm at the *same* index as the sum and
gives `log n − S ≥ −2`.

**The real bracket is now provable** — upper from §136 (`log n − S ≤ log σ₀`), lower from §139
(`log n − S ≥ −2`), giving `|log n − S| ≤ max(log σ₀, 2)`.  Then the norm assembly and the limit.

**Thirteen lemmas** for part (B) to date, all green.  The recurring failure mode across §§131, 133, 138
is now unmistakable: **index and shift direction in an inequality must be checked, not assumed** — the
three defects were respectively an identity containing the wrong variable (`log n` under a limit), a

dominated convergence; (ii) pass the uniform bound to the limit to get `DigammaGrowthBound σ₀` for
every `σ₀ > 0`.  Note `norm_Lseq_le` needs `σ₀ ≥ 1`; smaller `σ₀` comes from the recursion already
formalised in §§115/116.

## 142. The last mile for part (B): exact recipe, with the API located (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-e883bde9`, round 37.  **Audit result and recipe, no code committed.**

**Audit (§106 rule).**  `Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Gamma/Beta.lean` has
`GammaSeq_tendsto_Gamma` — **pointwise only**; there is no locally-uniform or derivative version
anywhere in Mathlib.  So the limit passage must be built.

**The good news: only *pointwise* derivative convergence is needed.**  `Complex.digamma = logDeriv Γ`,
`logDeriv (GammaSeq · n) s = deriv (Γ_n) s / Γ_n(s)`, and `Γ_n(s) → Γ(s) ≠ 0` for `Re s > 0`, so
`L_n(s) → ψ(s)` follows from **pointwise** `deriv (Γ_n) s → deriv Γ s` — no local uniformity, no
`TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn.deriv`.  That is a real simplification over the goal's stated plan.

**The three steps, with the API located.**

1. **Differentiate the integral.**  From `GammaSeq_eq_approx_Gamma_integral`
   (`Γ_n(s) = ∫_0^n (1−x/n)ⁿ x^{s−1} dx`), differentiate in `s`:
   `deriv (Γ_n) s = ∫_0^n (1−x/n)ⁿ x^{s−1} log x dx`.
   Use **`hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le`**,
   `Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/ParametricIntegral.lean:288`.  (This file, *not*
   `MeasureTheory/Integral/ParametricIntegral.lean` — the same grep-for-the-wrong-path trap as §128.)
   The `s`-derivative of the integrand is `(1−x/n)ⁿ · x^{s−1} · Complex.log x` via `deriv_const_cpow`
   built by `Complex.cpow_add` on `x^{s-1} = x^{(s-1)}`.
2. **Dominated convergence of the derivatives.**  Copy the structure of Mathlib's own
   `approx_Gamma_integral_tendsto_Gamma_integral` (`Beta.lean:271`): an `indicator (Ioc 0 n)`, the
   dominator `Real.exp (-x) * x ^ (re s - 1) * |log x|` (integrable for `re s > 0`; the extra
   `|log x|` is integrable against `exp(-x) x^{σ-1}`), and `tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence`.
   The target is `deriv Γ s = ∫_0^∞ e^{−x} x^{s−1} log x dx`, which Mathlib proves alongside
   `hasDerivAt_Gamma`.
3. **Pass the uniform bound to the limit.**  `norm_Lseq_le` (§141) gives
   `‖L_n(σ₀+it)‖ ≤ (log σ₀+20)(1+log(|t|+2))` for *all* `n` and `σ₀ ≥ 1`; `Tendsto` + continuity of
   `‖·‖` gives `‖ψ(σ₀+it)‖ ≤ (log σ₀+20)(1+log(|t|+2))`, i.e. `DigammaGrowthBound σ₀` for `σ₀ ≥ 1`.
   For `σ₀ ∈ (0,1)` use the recursion `ψ(s) = ψ(s+1) − s⁻¹` — **already formalised in §115**.

**Why I stop here.**  Step 1 is the only genuinely new development left, and it is API-heavy in the
manner that has consumed 2–4 rounds per lemma throughout (§§131–141).  With the ingredient list above
fully located, a successor can execute it directly; the mathematics is settled (§123) and 15 of the
16 lemmas are already committed.

`./check.sh --all` green over **28** files; 15 lemmas for part (B), all with footprint
`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

## 144. **Two finds that make step 1 almost free** (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-e883bde9`, round 39.  **Fifth "the tool was already in Mathlib" find — and the largest.**

Auditing for §143's step 1, I opened **`Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Gamma/Deriv.lean`** — an
entire file, never audited in this development — and **`Mathlib/Analysis/MellinTransform.lean`**.

**Find A — step 2 is free.**  `Gamma/Deriv.lean:67`:

```lean
theorem hasDerivAt_Gamma_of_re_pos {s : ℂ} (hs : 0 < s.re) :
    HasDerivAt Gamma (∫ t : ℝ in Ioi 0, t ^ (s - 1) * (Real.log t * Real.exp (-t))) s
```

That is *exactly* `deriv Γ s = ∫_0^∞ t^{s−1} log t · e^{−t} dt` — the target of §142 step 2, already
proved.  (§142 had it as "which Mathlib proves alongside `hasDerivAt_Gamma`" — it does, and it is
stated in the form needed.)

**Find B — step 1 needs no dominated convergence at all.**  `MellinTransform.lean:320`:

```lean
theorem mellin_hasDerivAt_of_isBigO_rpow (hfc : LocallyIntegrableOn f (Ioi 0))
    (hf_top : f =O[atTop] (· ^ (-a))) (hs_top : s.re < a)
    (hf_bot : f =O[𝓝[>] 0] (· ^ (-b))) (hs_bot : b < s.re) :
    MellinConvergent (fun t => log t • f t) s ∧
      HasDerivAt (mellin f) (mellin (fun t => log t • f t) s) s
```

Apply it to `f_n := fun x => if x < n then ((1 − x/n) ^ n : ℂ) else 0`.  Then
* `LocallyIntegrableOn f_n (Ioi 0)` ✓ (bounded, compactly supported);
* `f_n =O[atTop] (·^(-a))` ✓ for *any* `a` (eventually zero), so `hs_top` with `a := s.re + 1`;
* `f_n =O[𝓝[>]0] (·^0)` ✓ since `f_n → 1`, so `hs_bot` is exactly `hs : 0 < s.re`.

and `mellin f_n s = ∫_0^∞ x^{s−1} f_n(x) dx = ∫_0^n x^{s−1}(1 − x/n)^n dx = GammaSeq s n`
(by `GammaSeq_eq_approx_Gamma_integral`).  So **`deriv Γ_n s = mellin (log · • f_n) s` immediately** —
the whole `HasDerivAt.const_cpow` + parametric-integral derivation that §143 was grinding on is
**already packaged**.

**What actually remains** is then only the dominated-convergence comparison
`mellin (log · • f_n) s → mellin (log · • exp(−·)) s`, whose dominator is `x^{σ−1}|log x| e^{−x}`
(integrable for `σ > 0`) and whose integrands are dominated pointwise by `x^{σ−1}|log x| e^{−x}` via
`one_sub_div_pow_le_exp_neg`.  That is **step 2 of §142, not step 1**, and it is the same shape as
Mathlib's own `approx_Gamma_integral_tendsto_Gamma_integral` (`Beta.lean:271`) — a worked template.

**Consequence.**  §142's plan had step 1 as "the only genuinely new development left".  It is not new:
Mathlib packages it.  The remaining work is **one dominated-convergence lemma**, and then
`logDeriv Γ_n → logDeriv Γ` by continuity of division away from `0`.

**The pattern, fifth instance.**  §§106, 120/127, 128, 144: `LSeries/Nonvanishing.lean`,
`harmonic_le_one_add_log`, `SumIntegralComparisons.lean`, and now `Gamma/Deriv.lean`.  **Four separate
times, an "open problem" in this development was a file I had not opened.**  The only reason round 39
found it is that §143 forced me to state precisely *which* theorem I needed — and the name
`hasDerivAt_Gamma_of_re_pos` was then one grep away.

## 145. `logDeriv_GammaSeq` — third attempt, third revert, obstacles pinned (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-e883bde9`, round 40.

**Attempted again:** `logDeriv (GammaSeq · n) s = log n − ∑_{j<n+1} (s+j)⁻¹`.  This is the identity
that links §144's free `Mellin` derivative to the explicit `L_n`.  **Reverted**; `./check.sh --all`
green over **28** files.  (Earlier attempts: rounds 19, 20.)

**The three residual goals, recorded exactly:**

1. **Lambda vs product-of-functions.**  `logDeriv_prod` is stated for `logDeriv (∏ i ∈ s, f i) x`, i.e.
   a product *of functions*; the goal has `logDeriv (fun w => ∏ j, (w + ↑j)) s`.  The bridge is
   `show (fun w => ∏ j, (w + ↑j)) = ∏ j, (fun w => w + ↑j) from by funext w; simp [Finset.prod_apply]`
   — but `Finset.prod_apply` alone left the coercion `↑j` vs `↑(j : ℂ)` unresolved.
2. **`GammaSeq` unfolding.**  `rw [GammaSeq]` after `funext w` **does not close**, because `GammaSeq`'s
   definition writes `(s + j)` with `j : ℕ` coerced, while the goal has `(w + (j : ℂ))`.  Needs
   `push_cast`.
3. **`HasDerivAt.const_cpow` is a method, not a function.**  There is no `hasDerivAt_const_cpow`; the
   form is `(hasDerivAt_id s).const_cpow (Or.inl h)` — see the *worked example* at
   `Mathlib/Analysis/MellinTransform.lean:395`, which uses exactly
   `convert! ((hasDerivAt_id' y).sub_const 1).const_cpow (Or.inl ht') using 1`.

**Assessment.**  All three are plumbing, and all three now have their fix named — the shape of this
identity is fully understood after three encounters.  What I have not managed is to *converge* on it
in a single round, and each attempt costs one.  With 15 of 16 lemmas committed and the mathematics
settled (§§123, 125, 144), the remaining work is exactly:

  (i) this identity (fixes 1–3 above);
  (ii) the dominated-convergence comparison of §144, whose template is
       `approx_Gamma_integral_tendsto_Gamma_integral` (`Beta.lean:271`);
  (iii) `logDeriv Γ_n → logDeriv Γ` from `Γ_n → Γ ≠ 0` and (ii);
  (iv) apply `norm_Lseq_le` (§141) through the limit; reduce `σ₀ < 1` by §115's recursion.

**Method note, and the round's real lesson.**  The productive reversal in this goal has been
*audit-then-state* (§§106, 128, 144 each replaced a perceived gap with an existing lemma).  This round
did the opposite: it went straight to proof on an identity already known to be awkward, and paid a
round for it.  **The rule I should have applied: if a statement has failed twice, spend the next round
locating every lemma it needs before writing any proof.**

## 148. **`logDeriv_GammaSeq` committed — after five attempts** (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-e883bde9`, round 43.  **The identity that blocked rounds 19, 20, 40 and 41 is proved.**

**Proved** [`011/lean/GammaBounds.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/011/lean/GammaBounds.lean):

* **`logDeriv_GammaSeq`** — `logDeriv (GammaSeq · n) s = log n − ∑_{j<n+1} (s+j)⁻¹`, i.e.
  `deriv Γ_n s = Γ_n s · L_n s`.  Footprint `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`;
  `./check.sh --all` green over **28** files.

**What actually fixed it — and it was none of my five diagnoses.**

1. The lambda/product bridge is `funext w; simp only [Finset.prod_apply]` — §145 item 1. (My round-40
   claim that `↑j` was the obstacle was **wrong**.)
2. The `GammaSeq` unfolding is `funext w; simp only [GammaSeq, Pi.div_apply]` — my round-40 claim
   that `push_cast` was needed was **wrong**, and the `Pi.div_apply` I had been blaming for four
   rounds is *part of the fix*, not the problem.  The two function forms are in fact `rfl`-equal
   (verified in isolation), so the "normalform collision" I diagnosed in §146 **did not exist**.
3. **The real cause: `logDeriv_mul_const` already strips the constant factor.**  I had been writing
   `rw [logDeriv_div …, logDeriv_mul_const …, logDeriv_const, sub_zero, hsum]`.  The `logDeriv_const`
   then has *no occurrence to rewrite* — there is no `logDeriv (fun _ => a)` left — and `rw` aborts
   **the entire rewrite list**, so `logDeriv_div` never fired and the goal looked untouched.  Deleting
   `logDeriv_const, sub_zero` made the proof go through **on the first try**.

**The lesson, and it is the sharpest of the session.**  For four rounds I read the symptom —
"`logDeriv_div` produced nothing" — as a *matching* failure between normalforms, and invented three
plausible normalform explanations.  The actual mechanism was that **`rw` is all-or-nothing across a
list**: one inapplicable step silently discards every earlier step in the same `rw`.  The diagnostic
that found it was `trace_state` *between* steps — the goal after `rw [hfun]` was already
`logDeriv (n^·) s − logDeriv (∏…) s`, proving the rewrites had fired and that the failing step was
late in the list, not early.

**Rule (ninth): never diagnose a `rw` failure from the final goal; split the list and `trace_state`
between steps.**  A failing later step rewrites history for every earlier one.

**State of part (B): 16 lemmas committed**, all clean.  Remaining: (i) `deriv Γ_n → deriv Γ` — §144's
two finds plus one dominated-convergence lemma; (ii) `L_n → ψ`; (iii) the final assembly.

## 149. **The Mellin bridge is complete** (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-e883bde9`, round 45.  Session set to unlimited turns; the bridge was finished.

**Proved** [`011/lean/GammaBounds.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/011/lean/GammaBounds.lean):

* **`gammaKernel`** — the compactly-supported kernel `x ↦ if x ≤ n then (1−x/n)ⁿ else 0`;
* **`gammaKernel_eq_indicator`** — on `Ioi 0` it *exactly* equals the `Ioc 0 n`-indicator;
* **`mellin_gammaKernel`** — `mellin (gammaKernel n) s = GammaSeq s n` for `0 < re s`, `n ≠ 0`.

Footprints `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`; `./check.sh --all` green over **28** files.

**The design decision that made it work.**  Define the kernel with **`x ≤ n`**, not `x < n`.  Then on
`Ioi 0` it agrees with the `Ioc 0 n`-indicator *pointwise* — no a.e. argument, no
`Measure.restrict_restrict`, no measure-theoretic side conditions.  The earlier attempts all used
`x < n` and then had to repair the mismatch at `x = n` and at `x ≤ 0`; choosing the form that matches
`Iic`/`Ioc` removed the entire problem.  (Same species as §131/§133/§138: *pick the statement whose
shape matches the library's*, rather than proving the mismatch away.)

**Proof skeleton, now standard.**  `rw [mellin, GammaSeq_eq_approx_Gamma_integral,
intervalIntegral.integral_of_le]` puts both sides as `∫ in Ioc 0 n`; `setIntegral_congr_fun` applies
`gammaKernel_eq_indicator`; then two `← integral_indicator` rewrites and
`Set.indicator_indicator` + `Set.inter_eq_right` reduce it to pointwise equality of the integrands,
closed by `ring`.

**Consequence for the chain.**  §144's `mellin_hasDerivAt_of_isBigO_rpow` now applies to `gammaKernel n`
directly, giving `deriv Γ_n s = mellin (log · • gammaKernel n) s` — the next step — and
`GammaSeq s n = mellin (gammaKernel n) s` identifies the denominator.  The limit passage becomes
`mellin (log · • gammaKernel n) s → deriv Γ s`, a single dominated-convergence lemma.

**Proved** [`011/lean/GammaBounds.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/011/lean/GammaBounds.lean):

* **`deriv_GammaSeq_eq_mellin`** — `deriv (fun w => GammaSeq w n) s = mellin (log · • gammaKernel n) s`.

Footprints clean; `./check.sh --all` green over **28** files.

**The `min` trick.**  Rewriting the `if x ≤ n` kernel as `(1 − min x n/n)ⁿ` makes continuity
*definitional for `fun_prop`* — the `if` form would have needed `continuous_if_le` plus agreement of
the branches at `x = n`.  Third instance in this arc of **choosing the statement shape the library
already handles** (§§131/133/138/149).

## 151. Pointwise convergence and domination of the kernels (2026-10-13)

**Proved** [`011/lean/GammaBounds.lean`](research/twin-prime-parity/011/lean/GammaBounds.lean):

* **`tendsto_gammaKernel`** — for `t > 0`, `gammaKernel n t → ↑(exp(−t))` as `n → ∞`
  (via `Real.tendsto_one_add_div_pow_exp` + `⌈t⌉₊ ≤ n` making the `if` fire);
* **`norm_gammaKernel_le`** — `‖gammaKernel n t‖ ≤ Real.exp (−t)` for `t > 0`
  (via `Real.one_sub_div_pow_le_exp_neg`, located at
  `Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Exponential.lean:643` — inside `namespace Real`).

**The trick that avoided a long chore.**  §151 listed the dominator's integrability as "the only
genuinely new analytic obligation".  It came out in one round by bounding `|log t|` against *powers*

no `IsBigO` transfer, no little-o asymptotics — the split I had planned in §151 was unnecessary.

expecting is repeatedly already in the library, once the *statement* is recast into the shape the
library provides.

```lean
theorem digammaGrowthBound_of_pos {σ0 : ℝ} (hσ0 : 0 < σ0) : DigammaGrowthBound σ0
```

i.e. `∃ C > 0, ∀ t, ‖Complex.digamma (σ₀ + it)‖ ≤ C·(1 + log(|t|+2))` **for every `σ₀ > 0`**.
Footprint `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`; `./check.sh --all` green over **28** files;
**no `sorry`, no `axiom`** anywhere.

**The final chain, in four theorems:**
1. **`tendsto_Lseq_digamma`** — `n ↦ log n − ∑_{j<n+1}(s+j)⁻¹` tends to `Complex.digamma s` for
   `0 < re s`.  Assembled from `logDeriv_GammaSeq` (§148), `deriv_GammaSeq_eq_mellin` (§150),
   `tendsto_mellin_log_gammaKernel` (§154), `GammaSeq_tendsto_Gamma` and
   `Complex.Gamma_ne_zero_of_re_pos`, then `Tendsto.div` + `Complex.digamma_def`.
2. **`digammaGrowthBound_of_one_le`** — `DigammaGrowthBound σ₀` for `σ₀ ≥ 1`, by passing
   `norm_Lseq_le` (§141) through the limit with `le_of_tendsto`.
3. **`digamma_norm_le_strip`** — the *uniform* strip bound on `1 ≤ σ ≤ 2` with constant `log 2 + 20`
   (needed because `obtain` on the `∃ C` of `DigammaGrowthBound` yields an **opaque** constant, so no
   comparison of constants is possible through it).
4. **`digammaGrowthBound_of_pos`** — extend to all `σ₀ > 0` via §116's reduction
   (`digammaGrowthBound_of_stripBound_all`), which needed the uniform form for exactly that reason.

## 156. Part (A): audit and plan (2026-10-13)

Goal `goal-e883bde9`.  **Part (B) is done (§155); this is the last interface.**

**Audit result.**  Mathlib has **no** convexity/growth bound for `L` in the critical strip — only
`LFunction_isBigO_horizontal` (`LSeries/Nonvanishing.lean:336`), which is about `x → 0+` near
`Re = 1`, not a `|t|`-growth bound.  So part (A) must be built.  The tools are present:
* **`PhragmenLindelof.vertical_strip`** (`PhragmenLindelof.lean:275`) — the strip `a < re z < b`,
  with hypothesis `f =O[comap (|·| ∘ im) atTop ⊓ 𝓟 (re ⁻¹' Ioo a b)] fun z ↦ expR (B * expR (c * |z.im|))`
  for some `c < π/(b−a)` — i.e. *polynomial growth is allowed*;
* `DirichletLogDeriv.lean` already has the Euler-product log-derivative
  `LSeries (Λ·χ) s = −deriv(LSeries χ) s / LSeries χ s` (`σ > 1`) via
  `DirichletCharacter.LSeries_twist_vonMangoldt_eq`.

**The decomposition that reduces the work.**  `Λ_χ′/Λ_χ = (1/2)log N + γ′/γ + L′/L`, so
* `(1/2)log N` — constant ✔;
* **`γ′/γ` is `O(log(|t|+2))` — and that is exactly `DigammaGrowthBound`, proved in §155!**
  (`γ(s) = (N/π)^{(s+a)/2}Γ((s+a)/2)`, so `γ′/γ = (1/2)log(N/π) + (1/2)ψ((s+a)/2)`, any `σ₀ > 0` ✔.)
  **So part (B) feeds part (A)** — the interface closed today is precisely the archimedean input the
  other one needs;
* `L′/L` on `1/2 ≤ σ ≤ 1` — the single remaining piece, to be obtained from a convexity bound for `L`
  (via `vertical_strip`) and then a Cauchy/Hadamard estimate for the logarithmic derivative.

**Plan.**
1. convexity bound `L(σ+it) ≪ (q(|t|+2))^{(1−σ)/2+ε}` on `0 ≤ σ ≤ 1` via
   `PhragmenLindelof.vertical_strip` applied to a normalised `L` (boundary `Re = 1` from the Dirichlet
   series / §106 non-vanishing, boundary `Re = 0` from the functional equation
   `IsPrimitive.completedLFunction_one_sub`);
2. `γ′/γ` bound on the strip from §155;
3. `L′/L` bound on the zero-free parts of the strip from (1) + Cauchy;
4. assemble the **contour** integral bound `CriticalStripLogDerivBound` (§119).
